articles.title: I’ve run hundreds of miles testing dozens of running watches — these are the best for beginners and racers alike
articles.summary: I’ve tested dozens of running watches from Garmin, Coros, Amazfit, Fitbit, Apple and more. Here are my top picks for beginners, races and ultra-athletes alike.
articles.body: The best running watch can help you achieve your fitness goals, whether that’s completing a local 5K or a world-famous marathon. They can show you key metrics like time, pace, distance, heart rate and more during your run, and advanced training and recovery stats after your run is over. The thing is, they can be pricey, and with so many options on the market, it can be hard to figure out which one is best for your needs, regardless of whether you’re new to running or have been dominating races for years. I’ve tested running watches, fitness trackers and smartwatches for years so you don’t have to. Below I’m sharing the best ones for runners of all kinds. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best running watches of 2026 My top picks come from a mix of small and large brands like Coros, Amazfit, Garmin and Apple. I request running watches directly from brands — every watch on this list was loaned to me for testing purposes. I include key specifications like size, weight and battery life within the ‘What to Know’ dropdown. Best running watch overall I was shocked by how good the Coros Pace 4 is for runners — it’s a goldilocks watch that hits just the right mix of features and price to make it great for basically anyone. It serves beginners and marathoners alike — I never felt the need to “upgrade” as I progressed on my running journey. I love how lightweight and compact the Pace 4 is. Many running watches dwarf my small wrists, leading to a generally uncomfortable fit. The Pace 4 is small, but not too small, and has enough buttons that you can comfortably control the watch via touchscreen or buttons alone. Using the watch and the Coros app feels streamlined compared to Garmin, Amazfit and others. Sure, it doesn’t have as many lifestyle features (no tap-to-pay, no music streaming), but it puts running and training front and center, with an intuitive app that never feels cluttered or overwhelming. It takes my top spot because the value per dollar is unmatched. There are almost no running watches with features like dual-band GPS, route creation, course pacing and strategy, hill alerts, marathon training plans, recovery metrics and class-leading long battery life for $250. The closest comparison I can think of is the Garmin Forerunner 265, which is far more expensive. You can also choose between a silicone and a nylon strap at purchase (most brands make you buy one or the other afterwards), and it comes in an ultralight plastic version (linked above) and a lightweight aluminum version that costs just a little more. Best running watch for beginners If you are just starting out as a runner and have never owned a fitness tracker or smartwatch, the Fitbit Charge 6 is a great option. It’s small, subtle, and simple to use — I felt comfortable swiping through the watch and app after only a few minutes of use. The Fitbit software in particular is very straightforward, with less complicated features than other brands. The small size, while a blessing most of the time, is a bit of a mixed bag while running — you can only see one or two stats on your wrist during runs, less than competitors with bigger screens. Again, this watch is best for beginners. If you are planning to run a marathon, you will outgrow the Fitbit Charge 6 quickly — it has shorter GPS battery life, less advanced running metrics and minimal controls compared to my other recommendations. You can read more in my Fitbit Charge 6 review. Best budget running watch Amazfit is a budget-friendly brand that undercuts the competition on price, and the Active 3 Premium is a prime example of that. It has features runners, cyclists and anyone working out outdoors can appreciate, namely four buttons (two on each side), long battery life, and a durable (albeit fingerprint-y) metal case and sapphire crystal screen. The downside is software: The watch and watch app are less intuitive than other options on this list. The app has loads of useful features not often found at this sub-$200 price, including coaching plans, built-in running workouts, recovery times and offline maps and navigation, they just require patience to get up and running. Best premium running watch If you love running and spare no expense to get the best gear possible, check out the Garmin Forerunner 970. It’s Garmin’s most advanced, most premium running watch, fit for any task, from 5K to ultra-marathon. It’s bursting at the seams with features. First, it’s a GPS powerhouse: It’s arguably the most accurate watch on this list for distance, mapping and navigation with its multi-band GPS. Second, it has the most training, recovery, workout and course features of all our recommendations — so much so that it’s often overwhelming (especially when some training tools are only available on the Garmin Connect website, not the mobile app.) What keeps the 970 out of the top spot is price — it’s significantly more expensive than every other watch on this list. Garmin does make the lower priced Garmin Forerunner 570 and budget-friendly Garmin Forerunner 165, but the Coros Pace 4 is still a better value comparatively. You can learn more about the brand in my Garmin watch guide. Best running watch for battery life The sleeper hit of this list, the Suunto Race 2 is a battery life king that’s more sleek and user-friendly than its performance-focused marketing would suggest. The watch and mobile app are both clear, snappy and responsive, with detailed metrics and features that are not overwhelming. Maps and navigation are another standout (also clear, detailed and responsive); they load faster and pan quicker than on competitors like the Garmin Forerunner 970. But it’s battery life where the Suunto Race 2 laps the competition: It gets up to 55 hours of battery life doing dual-band GPS activities. Turn on battery saving features like tour mode and that number can reach up to 200 hours. If you love the Suunto aesthetic but want something smaller and cheaper for your local turkey trot, consider the Suunto Run instead. Best running watch from Apple If you’re an iPhone person, any Apple Watch can pull double duty as a great beginner running watch. Like Fitbit, it’s incredibly easy to use, but has more detailed running, health and sleep metrics — no subscription required. Its square screen is perfect for showing multiple metrics while running, and it easily syncs with your phone for controlling things like music or calls. Where it’s lacking compared to a traditional running watch is training and battery life. It doesn’t have nearly as many training features as our other picks, and the 18-hour battery life is miniscule compared to a Coros or a Garmin. (The Apple Watch Ultra 3 gets up to 42 hours, but costs far more, and is still dwarfed by other brands.) Best running watch from Google This Android smartwatch also works great as a running watch for most people for two reasons: software and accuracy. It has robust software that lets you do all the smartwatch stuff but also do things like build custom runs, with stages, intervals and more. It also has more in-depth training and recovery metrics than most smartwatches. Perhaps more important: it’s very accurate. It uses dual-band GPS and an advanced heart rate tracker to deliver consistent results, in my experience. It’s biggest miss for me is the lack of physical buttons — it’s harder to control running with sweaty hands or gloves on because of it. How I tested running watches I’ve been a runner for more than six years, and use smartwatches and fitness trackers to monitor stats during and after my runs. I test running watches for at least two weeks, using as many features as possible and comparing them to other watches. During testing, I typically wear two running watches (one on each wrist) so I can compare individual workouts across devices. I pay close attention to the following factors during testing: Comfort: A running watch is useless if it’s so uncomfortable I don’t enjoy wearing it. I wear each watch day and night to see if it becomes uncomfortable, disrupts my sleep or irritates my skin.GPS tracking: I compare distance, pace and map data between devices to see how consistent they are.Training features: I try out all the key training features each watch has to offer, noting how approachable and useful they are short and long term.Battery life: I make note of how often I have to charge each device, and how easy it is to use the included charger.Compatibility: Not every running watch works with every smartphone. I test and include options for both iPhone and Android users. How to shop for a running watch Shopping for a running watch is all about your needs and goals. Keep these key factors in mind as you shop: Size The best running watch is the one that fits your wrist. That can be hard to find, as many running watches only come in one size, and that size is often big. I have smaller wrists (about a 6-inch circumference), and have tested dozens of wearables, so I know that I prefer my running watches between 42 and 45 millimeters in size. You can get a good feel for this by going to a store and trying on running watches in person, noting how different watch sizes feel. Fleet Feet, REI and Dick’s Sporting Goods are good options for this. Features and goals More features isn’t always better. Brands like Garmin are the most impressive on paper because they can do the most things, but that can make them overwhelming to use in practice. Think about how you use technology, and what kinds of tech experiences you enjoy. Tech-averse or love simplicity? Go for simpler, streamlined options like the Coros Pace 4 or an Apple Watch. Data and app-obsessed? Advanced watches from Garmin are for you. This goes hand in hand with your goals — anyone trying to hit a PR marathon time will find advanced training features from Coros and Garmin useful. People just trying to log steps and get more active will get more than enough from Fitbit and Apple watches. Why trust NBC Selected? Harry Rabinowitz is a former reporter at NBC Selected who covered technology, fitness and the outdoors, including stories on workout headphones, walking shoes and point-and-shoot cameras. He’s been testing smartwatches, fitness trackers and running watches for years — he tries new models constantly, comparing them against previous versions and similar competitors. For this story, he leveraged his years of testing experience to pick the best running watches on the market today. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Menopausa: 7 sinais que merecem atenção e avaliação médica | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira alguns sintomas que podem aparecer nesta fase e que precisam ser levados ao consultório
articles.summary: Confira alguns sintomas que podem aparecer nesta fase e que precisam ser levados ao consultório
articles.body:
Atenção: Este é um conteúdo patrocinado pela plataforma PinkMed e as informações contidas não substituem avaliação médica individual.

A menopausa não começa necessariamente no dia da última menstruação. A chamada transição para essa fase pode ter início até 10 anos antes, período em que as oscilações e a redução dos hormônios podem provocar mudanças em diferentes sistemas do organismo.

Por isso, nem sempre os primeiros sinais percebidos pela mulher serão os conhecidos calorões. Alterações no sono, memória, humor, articulações, libido e saúde íntima também podem aparecer ao longo dessa fase.

O estrogênio é o hormônio que participa da manutenção de diferentes estruturas e funções do organismo, contribuindo para a saúde dos ossos e dos vasos sanguíneos, além de influenciar na qualidade da pele e dos tecidos genitais. A queda desse hormônio influencia diretamente na composição corporal, na massa muscular e também no bem-estar.

Um aspecto que pode chamar atenção na menopausa são as mudanças no peso. Segundo Fernanda Escobar (CRM/SC 25064 | RQE 15738), médica ginecologista, a mulher pode aumentar de 5 a 10 quilos nos primeiros 10 anos da menopausa.

Reconhecer essas mudanças é importante para que a mulher saiba quando procurar avaliação médica e possa receber orientações de acordo com as próprias necessidades.

“O cuidado nessa fase deve olhar não apenas para os sintomas atuais, mas também para prevenção e qualidade de vida futura. Cuidar da menopausa é também investir em longevidade saudável, força e autonomia”, afirma Fernanda Escobar.

Menopausa também pode afetar a saúde íntima

Entre as mudanças que podem acontecer durante a transição para a menopausa e após a última menstruação estão as alterações na vulva, na vagina e no sistema urinário. Esse conjunto de sintomas é conhecido como síndrome geniturinária da menopausa.

A redução dos níveis de estrogênio pode interferir na lubrificação e nas características dos tecidos da região íntima, provocando diferentes sintomas. Eles, porém, não aparecem da mesma maneira ou com a mesma intensidade em todas as mulheres.

Além disso, nem toda alteração íntima significa que a causa seja a menopausa. Infecções, doenças dermatológicas e outras condições podem provocar sintomas semelhantes. Por isso, a avaliação individualizada é importante antes de identificar a origem de qualquer desconforto.

Muitas mulheres deixam de falar sobre essas mudanças por vergonha ou por acreditarem que fazem parte do envelhecimento. No entanto, sintomas íntimos persistentes ou que interferem na rotina merecem atenção.

Os sintomas podem variar em intensidade e frequência. Algumas mulheres apresentam apenas um, enquanto outras percebem diferentes alterações ao mesmo tempo.

Entre os sinais que merecem atenção estão:

1. Ressecamento vaginal e menor lubrificação

A redução do estrogênio pode modificar a hidratação e a lubrificação da região vaginal. O resultado pode ser uma sensação de ressecamento ou desconforto, inclusive durante as relações sexuais.

Sensações de ardência, coceira ou irritação na região íntima também podem aparecer. Como esses sintomas não são exclusivos da menopausa, a investigação é importante para identificar a causa.

3. Dor ou desconforto durante a relação sexual

A redução da lubrificação e outras mudanças nos tecidos da região genital podem estar associadas ao desconforto durante a atividade sexual. Quando isso acontece, conversar com um ginecologista ajuda a identificar as possíveis causas.

4. Pequenos sangramentos depois da relação sexual

Qualquer sangramento depois da relação sexual merece atenção, principalmente após a menopausa. O sintoma não deve ser automaticamente associado à alteração hormonal e precisa ser investigado.

5. Aumento da urgência ou da frequência para urinar

A mulher pode perceber que precisa ir ao banheiro com mais frequência ou que a vontade de urinar surge de maneira mais urgente. Alterações urinárias podem fazer parte do quadro, mas também podem ter outras origens.

6. Ardência ao urinar ou infecções urinárias recorrentes

Desconforto ou ardência durante a urina e episódios recorrentes de infecção urinária também podem aparecer nessa fase. Ainda assim, não é correto considerar que toda infecção urinária recorrente seja causada pela queda hormonal.

7. Mudanças na sensibilidade e na vida sexual

Alterações no conforto, na sensibilidade e na experiência sexual também podem interferir na qualidade de vida. O impacto pode envolver autoestima, sono, bem-estar e relacionamento com o próprio corpo.

Quais tratamentos são indicados para as alterações íntimas?

O tratamento depende da causa e da intensidade dos sintomas. Após a avaliação ginecológica, podem ser indicados hidratantes e lubrificantes vaginais, fisioterapia do assoalho pélvico e terapias hormonais locais ou sistêmicas, quando não houver contraindicações.

Em situações específicas, também podem ser avaliados procedimentos ginecológicos íntimos, cirúrgicos ou não cirúrgicos, voltados a alterações funcionais ou anatômicas da região. Essas opções podem ser consideradas diante de queixas como desconforto, dor, flacidez dos tecidos, alterações provocadas pelo parto ou incômodo relacionado à anatomia íntima.

A escolha deve considerar o histórico clínico, os sintomas e as expectativas de cada mulher. Nem toda alteração exige um procedimento, e a indicação precisa ser definida individualmente após exame e avaliação médica.

A PinkMed é uma plataforma que conecta médicos especializados a pacientes que buscam por atendimento. No site, é possível obter informações sobre os especialistas, e agendar uma consulta com um(a) médico(a) parceiro(a) na sua região.

Para saber mais sobre tratamentos e procedimentos íntimos, além de consultar informações sobre profissionais e resultados publicados com finalidade educativa, acesse o site da PinkMed.

articles.title: Canal do Porto de Santos fica mais de 20h com navegação suspensa  | G1
articles.standfirst: Quatro cabos de energia, que pesam mais de três toneladas, foram removidos. A previsão é liberar o trecho ainda na tarde desta sexta-feira (30).
articles.summary: Quatro cabos de energia, que pesam mais de três toneladas, foram removidos. A previsão é liberar o trecho ainda na tarde desta sexta-feira (30).
articles.body:
O canal do Porto de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, está com a navegação parcialmente suspensa há mais de 20 horas nesta sexta-feira (30), após um guindaste atingir e romper quatro cabos de energia . Conforme apurado pelo g1 , a restrição afetou as operações de sete navios.

Os cabos, que pertencem à linha de transmissão da Usina Hidrelétrica de Itatinga e pesam mais de três toneladas, foram removidos. A previsão é que o trecho seja liberado ainda na tarde desta sexta-feira (30).

O acidente ocorreu na quinta-feira (29), quando um guindaste instalado em uma barcaça que prestava serviço para terminais atingiu a estrutura ( assista acima ). Após o ocorrido, a Capitania dos Portos determinou o fechamento de parte do canal por volta das 16h25.

Guindaste atinge e derruba cabos de energia no Porto de Santos, SP — Foto: g1 Santos

Segundo a Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS), que administra o maior complexo portuário do país, a suspensão na navegação afetou a operação de sete embarcações.

Ao todo, quatro navios precisaram ser reprogramados, pois deveriam entrar no complexo portuário nesta quinta-feira (29). Os outros três seguem aguardando liberação para sair do cais santista.

O gerente de Saneamento, Energia e Conservação da APS, Rafael Apolinário, informou que a operação de remoção dos cabos deve ser concluída ainda na tarde desta sexta-feira (30).

"Estamos tomando as providências para garantir a segurança da navegação e, o quanto antes possível, fazer a liberação do canal", afirmou.

Equipes realizam retirada dos cabos de energia derrubados por guindaste no Porto de Santos — Foto: APS/Divulgação

Segundo a APS, a navegação precisou ser interrompida no trecho do canal a partir do cais da Marinha, em direção às regiões do Centro, Alemoa e Ilha Barnabé.

Já a área entre o cais da Marinha e a Ponta da Praia está operando normalmente. Desta forma, a restrição não afeta as travessias de passageiros entre Santos e Guarujá.

Cabos de energia foram derrubados por guindaste no Porto de Santos — Foto: APS/Divulgação

O fornecimento de energia ao prédio da Autoridade Portuária não chegou a ser interrompido devido ao sistema de emergência mantido com a Companhia Paulista de Força e Luz (CPFL). "Ou seja, há sempre duas fontes de energia disponíveis", disse a APS.

Já os terminais utilizam energia privada e são socorridos com a energia vinda de Itatinga apenas em casos de eventual interrupção no fornecimento.

articles.title: MPF não confirma mortes de indígenas e apura ameaças e racismo em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Procurador da República, Marco Antônio de Almeida, afirma que vítimas de supostos assassinatos não foram identificadas como indígenas. Órgão também investiga ameaças contra comunidades tradicionais do estado.
articles.summary: Procurador Marco Antônio de Almeida diz que vítimas de mortes investigadas não foram identificadas como indígenas. MPF também apura ameaças contra comunidades tradicionais em MS.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) investiga denúncias de racismo e ameaças contra indígenas e quilombolas em Mato Grosso do Sul. O órgão também apurou denúncias feitas por indígenas nas redes sociais sobre supostos assassinatos de integrantes de comunidades em Naviraí . Após ouvir lideranças e consultar registros, o MPF não encontrou elementos que comprovassem que as vítimas pertenciam a povos indígenas.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o procurador da República Marco Antônio Delfino de Almeida, explicou que por se tratar de mortes de pessoas não indígenas, as invsestigações serão feitas pelo Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul (MPMS).

Conforme explicou o procurador, o MPF ouviu lideranças indígenas de Naviraí e consultou informações sobre a origem familiar das vítimas e registros de atendimento na rede de saúde indígena. A Polícia Federal segue investigando os casos.

Segundo Almeida, o primeiro passo foi verificar se as vítimas eram reconhecidas pelas comunidades indígenas da região. As lideranças consultadas disseram que não tinham conhecimento de que essas pessoas pertenciam aos grupos.

O procurador explicou que, segundo a Convenção 169 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT), a identidade indígena leva em conta o reconhecimento da própria pessoa como indígena e seu vínculo com a comunidade.

🔎A Convenção 169 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT) é um tratado internacional que estabelece direitos dos povos indígenas e tribais. O documento reconhece a importância da identidade cultural e da autoidentificação: a pessoa deve se reconhecer como indígena, e sua identidade deve ser considerada em conjunto com o vínculo e o reconhecimento pela comunidade à qual pertence. O Brasil ratificou a convenção em 2002.

Suposta manipulação de imagens e investigação

O MPF também investigou a origem familiar das vítimas, mas não encontrou informações que comprovassem vínculos com povos indígenas.

O MPF também consultou registros da Secretaria Especial de Saúde Indígena (Sesai) para saber se as vítimas haviam recebido atendimento na rede de saúde indígena. Segundo o procurador, não foram encontrados registros.

Com base nas informações levantadas, Almeida afirmou que imagens podem ter sido manipuladas ou retiradas de contexto para apresentar as vítimas como indígenas.

"Entendemos que houve, em tese, manipulação de imagens para que houvesse essa informação. Mas ela não guarda conexão com a realidade", declarou.

Segundo o procurador, as mortes continuam sendo investigadas pelo Ministério Público Estadual, já que o MPF não encontrou elementos que comprovem que as vítimas eram indígenas.

O MPF também investiga denúncias de ameaças e possíveis crimes de racismo contra comunidades tradicionais em Mato Grosso do Sul.

Um dos casos envolve a Aldeia Sassoró, em Tacuru, onde áudios que circularam nas redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagens mencionam a possibilidade de envenenar a água consumida por indígenas após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). O servidor municipal apontado como autor das declarações foi afastado do cargo.

Segundo Almeida, o órgão já identificou suspeitos de ameaçar comunidades quilombolas e pediu a abertura de um inquérito para investigar o caso.

O procurador afirmou que as denúncias devem ser investigadas tanto na área criminal, para identificar e punir os responsáveis, quanto na área cível, que pode resultar em medidas de reparação às vítimas. Segundo Almeida, as ameaças podem configurar crimes de ódio e racismo.

➡️A legislação brasileira prevê penas de prisão e multa para crimes de racismo e discriminação. A Lei nº 7.716/1989 estabelece punições para práticas de preconceito ou discriminação por raça, cor, etnia, religião ou procedência nacional. Dependendo da conduta, as penas podem variar de dois a cinco anos de reclusão. A Constituição Federal também considera o racismo um crime inafiançável e imprescritível, sujeito à pena de reclusão.

O procurador também falou sobre uma investigação de ameaças de envenenamento , conduzida pelo 6º Ofício da Procuradoria da República em Dourados .

Segundo o procurador, o MPF segue atuando na apuração das denúncias para esclarecer os fatos e buscar a responsabilização dos envolvidos em possíveis crimes de racismo e ameaças contra comunidades tradicionais.

articles.summary: Topdek Informática reúne placas de vídeo, SSDs e outros componentes para quem deseja montar ou atualizar um computador em Ciudad del Este.
articles.body:
Montar um PC gamer permite escolher componentes de acordo com os jogos, os programas e o desempenho desejado. Antes de comprar as peças, porém, é importante definir o objetivo do computador e estabelecer um orçamento, considerando não apenas os componentes individuais, mas também a compatibilidade entre eles.

O processador, a placa-mãe, a memória RAM, a placa de vídeo, o armazenamento e a fonte de alimentação trabalham em conjunto. Por isso, escolher as peças de forma equilibrada ajuda a aproveitar melhor o desempenho do equipamento.

Componentes para diferentes configurações

A placa de vídeo é um dos componentes mais importantes para quem pretende jogar em resoluções elevadas ou utilizar aplicações gráficas. A escolha deve considerar os jogos, a resolução do monitor e o nível de desempenho esperado.

O processador também influencia o resultado, enquanto a memória RAM e o armazenamento contribuem para o funcionamento do sistema e a execução de programas. Um SSD, por exemplo, pode reduzir o tempo de inicialização do computador e o carregamento de jogos e aplicativos.

Outro cuidado é verificar se as peças são compatíveis entre si, incluindo o formato da placa-mãe, o gabinete, a fonte e os requisitos de energia dos componentes.

Onde encontrar peças para PC gamer no Paraguai

A variedade de peças permite pesquisar alternativas para diferentes necessidades, desde computadores para jogos competitivos até máquinas voltadas a atividades profissionais e criação de conteúdo.

articles.summary: O Conexão Enem 2026 oferece revisões presenciais gratuitas no Shopping Riomar e dicas exclusivas na TV Sergipe para apoiar os candidatos na reta final das provas.
articles.body:

articles.title: Estiagem: Abastecimento de água é suspenso em comunidade da capital | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil da capital confirmou que problema administrativo provocou suspensão temporária do fornecimento de água no Panorama, que depende de caminhão-pipa neste período.
articles.summary: Defesa Civil da capital confirmou que problema administrativo provocou suspensão temporária do fornecimento de água no Panorama, que depende de caminhão-pipa neste período.
articles.body:
Em meio ao cenário de estiagem no Acre, o abastecimento de água da comunidade do Panorama, na capital Rio Branco , foi suspenso.

À Rede Amazônica e ao g1 , a Defesa Civil Municipal confirmou que um problema administrativo provocou a suspensão temporária do fornecimento de água às comunidades que dependem de caminhões pipa.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Rio Branco para saber quando o abastecimento deve ser retornado, além das ações da Operação Estiagem e, até o fechamento desta reportagem, não obteve retorno.

O presidente da associação de moradores do bairro Panorama, Armando dos Santos, disse que há cerca de 15 dias a água foi suspensa na região.

“Esse ano foi meio atípico. Todos os anos ela se estende até final de novembro, muitas vezes até dezembro e há 15 dias ela [o abastecimento de água] foi suspensa. Temos um problema muito sério de posto de captação através do solo, porque os poços aqui tem que ser bastante fundo e muitos são cavados a 6 metros e começam a esbarrancar. As famílias, por serem carentes, não tem como pavimentar esse poço e fica à mercê da sorte, faltou água não tem como procurar água mais funda”, disse.

Devido a seca, abastecimento de água é suspenso em comunidades de Rio Branco — Foto: De olho no rio/Prefeitura de Rio Branco

O governo federal liberou R$ 19 milhões para reforço às ações de enfrentamento à seca no Acre . Segundo Armando, sem água em casa, as famílias precisam recorrer à compra, mas o custo nem sempre cabe no orçamento.

“Alunos saindo sem tomar banho, comida não sendo feita por falta de água e crianças com dificuldade para consumir essa água para realmente matar sua sede. Hoje, um galão de água está custando aqui R$ 8. Então, as famílias não tem nem condição de comprar o ovo para comer, como é que vai comprar água”, afirmou.

Em média, 7 mil famílias dependem totalmente do abastecimento feito pela prefeitura — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

Em média, 7 mil famílias dependem totalmente do abastecimento feito pela prefeitura. De acordo com o coordenador da Defesa Civil de Rio Branco, o tenente-coronel Cláudio Falcão, a situação deve ser resolvida nos próximos dias.

“Por um problema administrativo, tivemos que fazer a suspensão momentânea dessa operação e informamos tudo ao gabinete do prefeito, à Secretaria de Articulação e estamos aguardando uma resposta do gabinete para tomar decisões mais efetivas”, explicou.

Além da suspensão do serviço, Falcão detalha que o órgão também enfrenta dificuldades para conseguir caminhões em um período de alta procura por esse tipo de veículo.

“Nós temos um plano de trabalho que foi encaminhado para o governo federal, que preconiza a alocação de caminhões. Nós estamos com muita dificuldade em alocar caminhões devido à alta demanda. Então, estamos também esperando por essa solução e entendemos, inclusive, toda a necessidade da comunidade”, detalhou.

No Acre, os 22 municípios tiveram situação de emergência reconhecida devido a estiagem . A medida permite que as prefeituras solicitem recursos para ações de resposta aos efeitos da seca.

Abastecimento de água é suspenso em comunidades rurais no Acre — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil Estadual, coronel Carlos Batista, a medida serve para fortalecer tanto as ações do estado como as dos municípios.

“No sentido de aquisição, de solicitação, por meio de planos de trabalho, de recursos complementares do governo federal para fortalecer as ações que já estavam em andamento. Houve o reconhecimento federal, a liberação desses recursos, o montante de um pouco mais de R$ 19 milhões em 15 planos de trabalho do estado, de mais de 14 municípios aqui do estado, e esses recursos já estão liberados. A fase agora é de executar esses recursos, fazer a aquisição desses insumos para entregar para aquelas populações mais afetadas”, informou.

Conforme o coordenador, o estado segue fazendo a entrega de insumos para a população para auxiliar neste período, principalmente as comunidades mais vulneráveis.

“Recentemente o estado entregou mais de 4 mil cestas básicas para os municípios entregarem para aquelas famílias que estão sendo mais impactadas. As comunidades mais afetadas são as extrativistas, as comunidades indígenas, os ribeirinhos e os pequenos produtores rurais. Então, são essas comunidades e aquelas pessoas que também são do CadÚnico, pessoas bem vulneráveis, todas elas estão sendo assistidas”, finalizou.

articles.title: After years of building her art business and a highway tyre blowout that made her rethink life, Australian mortgage lender Ka Po Ng quit her bank job in 2024 to pursue art full time
articles.summary: After a life-changing tyre blowout, Australian mortgage lender Ka Po Ng followed her artistic dreams, leaving her banking job to pursue art full-time. Discover her journey of transformation and creative success.
articles.body: A frightening experience on the road can change how a person thinks about the future. For Melbourne-based artist Candy Ng, whose legal name is Ka Po Ng, a tyre blowout during a highway drive became a turning point that prompted her to reconsider her priorities. In November 2024, after years of building her art business, much of it alongside full-time work as a mortgage lender, Ng resigned from her banking job to pursue art full-time, according to the About page on her own website, Candy Ng Art. The blowout was not the only reason for her decision. It was a catalyst that pushed her toward an ambition she had held for a long time.An early attempt at becoming a full-time artistTo understand why this decision felt different, it helps to look at her first attempt. According to her website, Ng first left finance to pursue art in 2020. Even though her banking job provided security, its stresses eventually led to burnout. Ng quit the banking sector and decided to test whether she could earn her living from art. Over the next seven months, she created abstract paintings and promoted them on Instagram to attract buyers. She later returned to the mortgage industry as a mobile mortgage banker while continuing to develop her art business. From the experience, she learned that to make art her career, she had to have much more than just passion. She needed a viable business model, a clientele and an idea of how costly it was going to be. Instead of quitting her artistic dreams, she kept working on her skills together with her job.Building an art business while working in bankingIn that role, she started earning a six-figure salary and got a company car. At the same time, Ng was broadening her artistic horizons in her spare time. In addition to painting, she has been able to offer services such as customer illustrations, event illustrations, engraving and Western and Chinese calligraphy. Such services helped her in various ways to make money from her creative abilities. As she became popular through her work, she started getting bookings and working with her customers. The growth of her artistic career meant she was better prepared to take the risk than she had been when she first tried to make a career out of her art. The importance of this preparation is that by quitting her job, she lost her regular salary.The highway incident that prompted reflectionIn 2024, Ng experienced a tyre blowout while driving, an incident she later described as a wake-up call that prompted her to reconsider her career and priorities. In her January 2025 account of her career change, Ng said her car started fishtailing, but she slowed down and pulled into a service lane as a large truck overtook her. She received roadside assistance after the tyre blowout, allowing her to continue her journey. Though Ng was lucky enough not to experience the result she was afraid of, the incident left an impression on her. On the trip back, Ng wondered what could have happened if she had died on that day and asked herself if she was making good use of her time.As Ng rated her experience, she called it a wake-up call. It made her think of how long she wanted to wait before giving up her art aspirations for a job that did not seem relevant anymore. However, the decision was not an impulsive response to the roadside incident. By then, she had spent years developing her art business, building savings and establishing customer relationships. Her previous experience of working full-time as an artist had also given her a clearer understanding of the risks.Resigning to pursue art full timeNg left the banking job in November 2024, motivated by the perspective she gained after the highway incident. This time Ng was more ready to make the change because her business in art had grown from being experimental. The variety of services offered, growing number of clients and management of financial risks that came with running the artistic business were factors that played a major role in helping her make the right decision. She could spend her working hours painting and performing at live events.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 1929: Roland Callingham opened his family’s miniature world; Bekonscot remains the world’s oldest surviving model village
articles.summary: Discover Bekonscot Model Village in Beaconsfield, the oldest surviving model village since 1929, featuring six miniature villages and a 10-mile railway. Perfect for family fun and charity support!
articles.body: By the late 1920s, London accountant Roland Callingham’s model railway had outgrown the family home. After his wife objected to the trains indoors, he moved the hobby into the garden of their house in Beaconsfield, Buckinghamshire. The railway and surrounding miniature landscape gradually grew into Bekonscot Model Village, which opened to visitors in 1929 and continues to operate today.Callingham first created the railway for private family entertainment. As the garden layout grew, visitors encouraged him to open it to the public. Guinness World Records identifies Bekonscot as the world’s oldest surviving example of a model world. Its profile describes six miniature villages, hundreds of buildings and a railway with a reported length of 10 miles. That figure should be understood as a scale equivalent, not ten miles of physical track. At a 1:32 scale, ten miles at full size would correspond to about 1,650 feet of model track. The attraction opened to visitors in August 1929.An interest that expanded beyond the houseThe story began before the model village opened to the public. Callingham had planned an indoor model railway by 1926, then began work on a garden swimming pool in 1927. A historical dossier from the Buckinghamshire Gardens Trust records that he used mounds of soil from the pool excavation to build the first model houses. The railway moved outdoors in 1928, and the landscape developed with rockeries, paths, water features and additional buildings.The name Bekonscot combines Beaconsfield, where Callingham lived, with Ascot, where his friend James Shilcock lived. Callingham worked with head gardener Tom Berry, Mr Clark and other household staff to extend the layout. The attraction grew over several years as more stations, houses and landscape features were added. Its early public days also raised money for charity.A village in miniatureBekonscot presents an imagined version of England, although many of its buildings draw on real places. The village buildings are roughly 1:12 scale, or one inch to one foot, while the railway uses a smaller 1:32 scale. The difference is intentional: the attraction was designed to be playful and full of character, rather than to follow one consistent scale. Today it contains more than 200 miniature buildings, along with thousands of figures, animals and vehicles. The Buckinghamshire local heritage record confirms the different scales and explains that strict proportional accuracy was not Callingham’s main aim.Callingham prioritised enjoyment and character over exact scale. The miniature residents stand about 10 centimetres tall, and a team of twelve maintains the attraction throughout the year, with additional staff during the summer.Bekonscot initially changed with the times, adding modern buildings and vehicles, but in 1992 its managers chose to restore a 1930s setting. Princess Elizabeth marked her eighth birthday with a visit in April 1934, accompanied by Queen Mary and her younger sister, Princess Margaret, who was three at the time. Elizabeth returned for her tenth birthday in 1936 and visited again later. Some models came from other attractions: the cottages in Greenhally were moved from Ramsgate Model Village and restored in 2003. Bekonscot also helped inspire later miniature attractions, including Madurodam in the Netherlands, which opened in 1952, and Legoland in Denmark, which opened in 1968.Built to raise money for charityBekonscot attracted coverage in newspapers, newsreels and magazines as visitors came to see the miniature landscape. Money from public visits went to charitable causes, and a formal association was established in 1934 to manage the attraction and distribute surplus income. Callingham died in 1961. The Church Army took over the village’s operation in 1978, and the site is now run by the Roland Callingham Foundation, which distributes profits to other charities. Today, the Roland Callingham Foundation operates Bekonscot and uses profits to support charitable causes. Opened to visitors in 1929, the attraction grew from Callingham’s garden railway into six miniature villages. It remains a carefully maintained snapshot of rural England as imagined in the 1930s.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India should arm Afghan Taliban against Pakistan: Sushant Sareen
articles.summary: India should consider formally recognising the Taliban government in Afghanistan and providing it with military assistance to counter Pakistan, strategic
articles.body: India should consider formally recognising the Taliban government in Afghanistan and providing it with military assistance to counter Pakistan, strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen has argued, calling for a rethink of New Delhi’s approach to its western neighbourhood.Speaking on Faultline with Ananya Dasgupta on Times Axis, Sareen said India should not allow international consensus to dictate its Afghanistan policy. He argued that if Pakistan was using military force to pressure the Taliban, India should consider helping the Afghan regime defend itself.“If the Afghan Taliban are going to be bullied by the Pakistanis… then maybe we should help them militarily,” Sareen said. “So that they can also hit back.”He went beyond making a general case for military assistance, suggesting that India consider supplying Afghanistan with anti-drone systems, drone technology and missile capabilities.“If you can give them some anti-drone systems to the Afghans, if you can give them maybe some drone technology, which will help them fight back, maybe give them some missile systems or, you know, long-range rocket systems,” Sareen said.“Why not? I think we should consider it so that at least the Pakistanis cannot, you know, bully somebody into submission,” he added, arguing that India needed to be more willing to take risks if it wanted to project power internationally.Sareen’s argument comes against the backdrop of growing tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban, once backed by Islamabad but now increasingly unwilling to follow its instructions. The conflict has exposed the limits of Pakistan’s long-standing effort to exercise strategic influence over Afghanistan.Sareen said India should also reconsider its refusal to formally recognise the Taliban government, which came to power in 2021. He argued that recognition need not mean approval of the regime’s ideology or policies.“Recognition does not mean endorsement,” he said, pointing out that countries maintain diplomatic relations with governments whose actions they do not necessarily agree with.According to Sareen, the Taliban are the de facto rulers of Afghanistan and India already has a degree of engagement with them. He questioned why New Delhi should continue to hold back from formal recognition simply because other countries have not changed their position.Sareen said New Delhi should make its own assessment of what serves Indian interests, rather than remain constrained by concerns about how other countries might react.“The world doesn't ask us for our opinions before they start doing things,” he said.Sareen believes Pakistan’s Afghan strategy has backfired. Islamabad once viewed the Taliban as a means of securing influence in Afghanistan, but the relationship has turned adversarial as the Taliban has asserted its own interests.Explaining the mistake in Pakistan’s calculations, Sareen said Islamabad had mistaken a temporary alliance with sections of the Afghan population for lasting control.“You can rent an Afghan, you can't buy him,” he said, adding that the Afghans acted in Pakistan’s interests only as long as it suited them. Once they gained greater agency, they began pursuing their own priorities.Pakistan accuses the Taliban of providing sanctuary to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), whose attacks have targeted the Pakistani state. The Taliban, in turn, has resisted pressure from Islamabad and accused Pakistan of backing groups opposed to its rule.Sareen also discussed Pakistan’s interest in the Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip of Afghan territory that could provide direct connectivity to Central Asia. He said Pakistan appeared to see control of the corridor as a way to gain strategic leverage over the Taliban, but warned that such a move could invite retaliation.For India, Sareen argued, the question is whether the deteriorating relationship between Pakistan and the Taliban creates an opportunity to protect its own strategic interests. He urged New Delhi to consider both diplomatic recognition and military assistance, while acknowledging that a more assertive role would carry risks.His proposal raises a difficult question for Indian policymakers: could a former Pakistani ally now become a strategic counterweight to Islamabad — and is New Delhi prepared to act on that possibility?You use AI every day. articles.title: An Indiana mother was ordered to pay $21,020 in attorney fees amid a custody dispute, then told that no further hearings would be held until she paid; an appeals court ruled on October 28 that the restriction was improper but upheld the fee award
articles.summary: An Indiana appeals court ruled on Wednesday, October 28, that a trial judge cannot stop a custody case from moving forward simply because a parent has not
articles.body: An Indiana appeals court ruled on Wednesday, October 28, that a trial judge cannot stop a custody case from moving forward simply because a parent has not paid legal fees. In a memorandum decision, the appeals court upheld the fee orders against the mother but struck down the condition that barred all further hearings until she paid the $21,020 in attorney fees.A custody battle that began more than five years agoThe custody battle began in 2021, when the father filed a paternity action concerning his two young children. The children were born out of wedlock in July 2017 and November 2018. The parents lived together until February 2020. That August, the father faced a criminal case over alleged domestic violence against the mother, and a criminal court barred him from contacting her and the children.The father filed for paternity in February 2021. About five months later, on July 26, the court confirmed that he was the children's father. It granted the mother sole legal and primary physical custody while the proceedings continued. It also granted the father supervised parenting time and ordered him to pay child support. In April 2022, the parties agreed to increase the father's unsupervised parenting time in stages. However, in November or December 2022, the mother took the children and left the court's jurisdiction, and their whereabouts became unknown. The father filed a contempt petition, and the children's guardian ad litem recommended that he be granted emergency custody. In January 2023, the judge ruled that the mother's behaviour had endangered the children and constituted a material change in circumstances. The father was granted temporary custody, while the mother was found in indirect contempt and allowed supervised visits.The court also found that the mother was a flight risk and posed a danger to the children's emotional well-being. She was ordered to undergo a psychological evaluation and anger-management assessments, and to complete the recommended treatment before she could progress towards unsupervised visits with her children. The mother was ordered to repay $1,448.34 in child support overpayments and pay $208 a week. The father was granted sole custody in February 2024.Attorney fees piled upAbout four months later, the father filed a contempt petition. He said the mother had not paid child support as ordered by the court and requested sanctions, including attorney fees. The court ordered the mother to pay the father $10,000 as a sanction. Later that year, she was also ordered to pay another $1,500 for contempt of court orders. Her child support arrears reached $11,708.34.The mother later approached the court seeking to change custody and child support arrangements. The trial court said her July 2024 request to change custody, parenting time and child support was “bordering on the frivolous”, as she had only recently started transitioning to supervised, in-person visits. In March 2026, the court ordered her to pay $15,000 in preliminary fees. She also owed $6,020 in sanctions for unpaid child support, a deposition she had cancelled at the last minute and a motion she had withdrawn just before a hearing.The court was not convinced by the mother's financial claims. She could not provide an exact figure for her income, but the court estimated it at $30,000 to $40,000 a year. It also pointed to a $70,000 settlement she had received, financial assistance from family members and the fact that her landlord was her own mother. The court said it found her income and expenses difficult to reconcile and concluded that she had the ability to pay both her fees and her child support.The trial court also ruled that it would not schedule any further hearings until the mother paid the attorney fees. Following this decision, the mother appealed the fee awards and the suspension of further hearings. The appeals court ruled that the trial court could not make further hearings conditional on the mother paying the attorney fees. It said such awards are money judgments and must be enforced through ordinary collection procedures under Indiana Trial Rule 69, rather than through contempt powers or by blocking access to further hearings. The appeals court reversed the part of the trial court's order that halted hearings until the mother paid the attorney fees. However, it did not overturn the $21,020 fee award. The father can still seek a money judgment and pursue appropriate collection proceedings to recover the amount.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: DEHRADUN: A chopper that belonged to Trans Bharat Aviation crashed into a hillside near Chai village around 2.20pm while flying from Badrinath to Dehradun.Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel rushed to the spotThe wreckage of a helicopter that crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday has been found. Chamoli SP Surjit Singh Panwar confirmed that all six people on board the helicopter have died and their bodies found. with all six people on board, including the pilot, feared dead, officials said.The helicopter, carrying five passengers and a pilot crashed near Chai village.The aircraft, operated by private company Trans Bharat Aviation, crashed into a hillside near the JP Power House, the district administration said.It was not immediately clear whether the helicopter was carrying passengers returning from the Badrinath shrine.Helicopter lost contact near Joshimath; what we know so far?According to sub-inspector Manohar Kanyal of Joshimath police post, information was received from the Joshimath Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) at 2.21pm that a helicopter had reportedly made a crash landing above Chai village in the Joshimath area.Also read: Wreckage of crashed helicopter found near Joshimath; all 6 on board feared dead (Video)Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) personnel informed officials that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter was showing near the Army camp above Chai village.The Joshimath and Pandukeshwar teams of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) left for the spot at 2.24pm.Pilot, five passengers on boardThe helicopter, bearing call sign VT-HCX, was being operated by Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt Ltd.It had taken off from Badrinath at approximately 1.14pm for Sahastradhara heliport in Dehradun before losing communication while flying over the Joshimath valley.According to UCADA, six people, including the pilot, were on board the helicopter. They have been identified as:Pilot: Capt HimanshuPassengers: Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K and H S NatrajaAs a precautionary measure following the incident, the entire fleet of Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt Ltd has been grounded, UCADA said.'Monitoring rescue operation'Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said he was closely monitoring the situation and had directed officials to ensure that critically injured passengers were immediately shifted to a higher-level medical facility.In a post on X, Dhami said, "Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF."I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers."Crash amid rain and snowfall in UttarakhandThe crash comes as several parts of Uttarakhand experience adverse weather conditions, with rainfall and snowfall reported across the state.Kedarnath Dham witnessed the season's first heavy snowfall following continuous snowfall since Thursday. The surrounding hills were covered in a thick blanket of snow, while temperatures in the region dropped.Dr CS Tomar, director of the Meteorological Centre in Dehradun, said rainfall activity was expected to continue over the next few days, particularly in the hilly districts, with light to moderate showers likely at several places.Speaking to ANI, Tomar said heavy rainfall was recorded at eight to nine places across the state on October 29, particularly in Uttarkashi, Tehri and Haridwar districts. He added that similar weather conditions were expected on Friday, with higher chances of rainfall activity in the Kumaon region.“Tomorrow, on the 31st, chances of light to very light rain will persist, especially in the hilly districts. Similarly, on the 1st and 2nd (of November), light to very light rain may be witnessed at isolated places, particularly in our northern hilly districts,” he said.Districts on alert as weather forecast continuesIn view of the weather forecast, district administrations have been placed on alert to ensure the safety of pilgrims and commuters.On Thursday, District Magistrate Prashant Arya directed the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) to remain in alert mode to monitor weather conditions and oversee precautionary measures.Authorities are also monitoring road conditions and the Gangotri and Yamunotri shrines through live CCTV cameras.The administration has appealed to devotees and pilgrims to take precautions against the cold and follow advisories issued by the administration and police.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: 'I will be present in court': Anant Singh to surrender by Dec 1 after SC cancels bail; accuses Neeraj Kumar of plotting case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Friday said he would surrender before the court by December 1 in compliance with the Supreme Court's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Friday said he would surrender before the court by December 1 in compliance with the Supreme Court's order cancelling his bail in the Dularchand Yadav murder case.He accused newly elected JD(U) MLC Neeraj Kumar of orchestrating the case against him and claimed that he had been deliberately implicated.Reacting to the Supreme Court's decision, Singh said he had faith in the judiciary and would abide by its directions. He also expressed confidence that he would be granted bail again."We will surrender. The court is not our enemy; whatever the court has decided is acceptable to us. The court will grant us bail again later. We have faith in the judiciary. We always had faith, and we still have faith today," Singh told reporters in Patna.Asked when he would surrender, the Mokama MLA said, "Why should I surrender early? I have full faith in the court and the judiciary. On whatever date is designated for me, I will be present in court."He subsequently confirmed that he would appear before the court on December 1.Singh alleged that Neeraj Kumar was behind the legal action against him and had ensured that his name was included in the murder case."This incident was orchestrated by Neeraj Kumar. First, from 3 kilometres away, he got my name added to the Dularchand murder case. After that, when I had been on bail here for six months, Neeraj took the case to Delhi. We only found out after everything had already transpired. They never issued any notice or informed us of anything; they did everything behind the scenes," he alleged.Asked whether he believed the Supreme Court's decision was the result of Neeraj Kumar's opposition, Singh said, "No, we don't believe that. You people claim the government did it--we don't accept that. Neeraj did it."He also accused Neeraj Kumar of being behind Yadav's murder and claimed that false witnesses had been brought forward to implicate him.“Neeraj got Dularchand murdered himself. He orchestrated it to immediately implicate Anant Singh and send him to jail. He brought false witnesses from his own locality, made them testify,” Singh alleged.Anant Singh recounts events leading to murderRecounting the events of October 30, 2025, Singh claimed that he was campaigning for votes when his convoy crossed paths with a vehicle carrying Dularchand Yadav, who was supporting a Jan Suraaj Party candidate."During the election, we were out asking for votes. There was a Jan Suraaj candidate, and Dularchand was in that vehicle. As we were returning after campaigning, we crossed paths with Dularchand on the road. After that, he went his way, and we went ours. When we had travelled about 4 to 5 kilometres, news spread that a clash had erupted right where we had just eaten," he said.Singh maintained that he learnt about Yadav's murder only after returning from campaigning in another village.According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran him over with an SUV. Singh has denied the allegations and previously claimed that Jan Suraaj supporters attacked his convoy first.Singh links expulsion to dispute with Neeraj KumarThe expelled MLA also linked his removal from the JD(U) to his differences with Neeraj Kumar, saying the party leadership had acted in support of the MLC."The party claims we opposed the party--we did not oppose the party, we opposed Neeraj," he said, referring to his campaign for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh against the JD(U)'s official nominee Neeraj Kumar in the Patna Graduates' constituency MLC election.Singh expressed confidence in former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, claiming that the developments would not have taken place had the JD(U) leader been in good health and actively involved in party affairs."I firmly believe that had Nitish Kumar ji been in good health and conscious of things, this would never have happened. The party wouldn’t have tossed me out like a fly from milk. Now that they have expelled me, the party will reap what it sows. They will struggle even to open their account," Singh said.Asked if he considered the matter a case of political vendetta, he said, “No, it isn’t politics. It is personal. It’s Neeraj. And the party backed Neeraj.”Singh said he would not approach any political leader for intervention and would follow the court's directions."I will not go to anyone regarding this matter. Nowhere at all. Whatever the court directs, I will abide by the court's word. If the court summons me, I will go to court," he said.On the multiple cases registered against him, Singh said, “Deceitful people keep implicating me, and I keep getting justice from the courts. By count, there may be 60 or 70 cases. When the judges examine the facts, they will deliver justice to me. I have done nothing wrong.”Supreme Court cancels bailEarlier on Friday, the Supreme Court cancelled the bail granted to Singh by the Patna High Court on March 19, 2026, and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the High Court had erred in granting bail without adequately considering the gravity of the offence and Singh's criminal antecedents. The bail order was challenged by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of the deceased.The development comes days after the JD(U) expelled Singh and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years, citing anti-party activities. Following the action, the Bihar government removed Neelam Devi from her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee and withdrew her Minister of State rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.The party has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the Anti-Defection Law.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Kerala passenger received ₹1 less on his cancelled train ticket and sued IRCTC; two years later, the consumer court ordered the railway corporation to pay ₹3,100 in compensation.
articles.summary: On receiving ₹1 less, a Kerala passenger sued the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) and ended up winning the refund and more in a
articles.body: On receiving ₹1 less, a Kerala passenger sued the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) and ended up winning the refund and more in a legal battle at the local consumer commission. The Kasaragod District Consumer Commission ordered the railway ticketing corporation to pay the passenger ₹3,100, along with the original residual amount. The rules that applied to the passenger, who booked and cancelled the ticket in 2024, have now been updated.The claimant cancelled his ticket on August 17, 2024, more than 48 hours before the scheduled journey on August 20, 2024. He booked an AC three-tier train ticket for ₹553 on August 11. The complaint mentions that IRCTC deducted ₹180 as cancellation charges and 5 per cent GST, which amounted to ₹9. As calculated, the refund amount came up to ₹341; however, IRCTC refunded only ₹340. This left a shortfall of ₹1.The shortfall caused the complainant confusion and mental distress. This incident caused a breach of trust towards India's primary railway organisation. His demands were ₹1 lakh for confusion, ₹1 lakh for breach of trust, ₹5,000 for litigation costs and the ₹1 shortfall.The commission rejected IRCTC's counter-argument because it was barred by limitation. It was noted that IRCTC did not attempt to justify the ₹1 shortage at the time of the refund. Failing to refund the exact amount was both a deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice. This created a liability for the organisation to refund the deficiency and pay additional compensation. The order by the commission mentioned, "Just because one rupee is paid less, the said fact really counts and the complainant is entitled to Rs 100 as compensation. Complainant is also eligible for the cost of litigation fixed as Rs 3,000."The complainant's demands were partly granted. The ₹1 was compensated by paying Rs 100, and additionally, the consumer forum directed IRCTC to pay Rs 3,000 for litigation costs."...complaint is allowed in part opposite party directed to refund Rs 1 with 9% interest from date of cancellation of date of ticket that is 17.08.2024 till realisation and Rs 100 towards compensation for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices and Rs 3000 as cost of litigation to the complainant within 30 days," the commission, chaired by Krishnan K, ordered.New Cancellation Policy of Indian RailwaysIndian Railways has modified its cancellation and refund policy for confirmed tickets, with the revised rules coming into effect in March 2026. Under the new rules, all cancellation time windows have been increased, giving passengers less flexibility to cancel tickets at the last minute. Earlier, a full refund, after deducting the applicable flat cancellation charge, could be availed if the passenger cancelled tickets more than 48 hours before departure. Now, to get the highest possible refund, tickets must be cancelled more than 72 hours before departure. Thus, the amount refunded to the Kerala passenger would have differed had the new rules applied to his cancellation.Even the 25% and 50% deduction windows have also changed, moving from 48-12 hours to 72-24 hours and from 12-4 hours to 24-8 hours, respectively. Finally, the no-refund window has doubled from the earlier four hours to eight hours. Fully waitlisted e-tickets are automatically cancelled after chart preparation if all passengers remain waitlisted, subject to applicable clerkage deductions. One exception is confirmed Tatkal tickets, which generally receive no refund upon cancellation. However, passengers are eligible for a full refund if the Railways cancels the train.Thus, please plan your journeys ahead of time and avoid any last-minute changes to your plans. Indian Railways' revised policy means passengers may receive a lower refund for modifications made closer to their travel dates.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1884, two Renaissance plaques disappeared from public view after an auction; 142 years later, they were identified in an English family's hallway and sold for more than £100,000 in October 2026
articles.summary: Two 16th-century Italian Renaissance maiolica plaques that disappeared into a private collection in 1884 have sold for £100,000 at auction.
articles.body: Two 16th-century Italian Renaissance maiolica plaques that disappeared into a private collection in 1884 have sold for £100,000 at auction. The artworks were recently found hanging in the hallway of an English family home. The ceramic pieces were made in 1536 by well-known Italian artist Francesco Xanto Avelli. They had been hanging unnoticed for decades in a house in Dorset. The owners did not know their historical importance or value until they emailed a photograph to specialist auction house Woolley and Wallis in Salisbury, Wiltshire. The plaques were sold as two separate lots during a specialist auction of British and European ceramics. Together, they reached a total hammer price of £100,000, solving a mystery that had lasted 142 years.Rediscovery in a Dorset hallwayThe story of their return to the art market began when the owners decided to ask experts about the decorative plaques hanging on their wall. After looking at the digital photographs sent by the family, specialists at Woolley and Wallis quickly recognised the work of Xanto, one of the most famous ceramic artists of the Italian Renaissance. According to research published by Woolley and Wallis, both plaques carry the artist's signature initials, "F.X.R." They also have numbers showing that they are pieces 4 and 10 from a famous series of artworks telling the story of Cyrus the Great, the founder of the Achaemenid Empire. "When I opened the email containing images of the two plaques, I could hardly believe what I was looking at," said John Axford, chairman and European ceramics specialist at Woolley and Wallis, in statements released before the auction. "To find two lost pieces from such a famous series hanging quietly in a family hallway is the sort of discovery every auctioneer dreams about."Provenance tracing back to 1884The two plaques are part of a large series of around 39 maiolica panels painted by Xanto in 1536. At the time, he was working in Urbino, an important centre for Italian ceramics. Xanto was born in Rovigo around 1487. He became famous for his colourful tin-glazed ceramics, which showed scenes from classical mythology, ancient history, and biblical stories. Records from past auctions, studied by art historians, confirm that the two plaques were last seen at a public auction in London in 1884. They were bought at that sale by General Augustus Henry Lane Fox Pitt Rivers, a well-known 19th-century archaeologist, collector, and founder of the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford. After General Pitt Rivers died, the plaques stayed in his family. They were passed down through several generations until they reached his descendants in the West Country region of South West England. Over the next 140 years, the family gradually forgot where the artworks came from. The plaques were eventually treated as ordinary wall decorations and remained in the hallway until experts recently identified their importance.Historical significance and museum tiesItalian Renaissance maiolica pieces of this quality, with such clear historical records, are extremely rare outside major museum collections. Xanto's Cyrus the Great series is well documented in art history books, but very few complete panels from the series remain in private collections. According to information provided by Woolley and Wallis, two other matching plaques from the same 1536 series are held in the permanent collection of the Louvre Museum in Paris. They are listed under accession numbers OA9028 and OA9029. The tin-glaze method used by Xanto required great skill. Artists painted colours onto a glaze before it was fired. The pigments were absorbed immediately, which meant there was no chance to correct mistakes. Despite spending decades hanging in an open hallway, the rediscovered Dorset plaques have kept their bright colours and fine details. These include vivid blues, rich copper-lustre shades, and carefully painted details of the human body. The successful auction at Woolley and Wallis shows that historic English country homes can still reveal valuable lost treasures from Europe's artistic past.You use AI every day. articles.title: Royal Enfield Nirvik riding gear review: The good and the not-so-good
articles.summary: Good riding gear rarely gets noticed on a short ride.
articles.body: Good riding gear rarely gets noticed on a short ride. It’s only after a few days of heat, dust, cold and several hundred kilometres that you figure out what works and what doesn’t. This year’s Royal Enfield Himalayan Odyssey gave me that chance. I rode in the Nirvik jacket, the Nirvik trousers and the Wanderer shoes for the whole expedition.This test loop threw every possible condition at our kit. We started in the blistering heat past Chandigarh, then bounced straight into frigid mountain mornings, sketchy gravel, river crossings and endless rock fields heading up to Umling La. It was a proper trial by fire. Here’s how everything survived.Royal Enfield Nirvik V3 Riding Jacket: Safe, practical, and a bit heavyThe fit was the first thing that struck me. The jacket sits well on the body, without feeling baggy or tight, and it looks premium too. The olive colour looks very decent, the stitching is neat, and the fabric feels like it can take a beating. After days of rough riding, I didn’t see any loose threads or signs of wear.What it offers: The body is made of 500D nylon, with 600D Cordura at the high-impact areas, which is where abrasion resistance matters most. Protection comes in the form of CE Level 2 armour at the shoulders, elbows and back, plus CE Level 1 at the chest. The armour is a mix of RE Ergo Protech and Norman Tech protectors.I’m fine never testing the armor in a crash, but it gives great peace of mind when the road drops off into a canyon. It sits comfortably without digging in, while the pockets are insanely practical. I easily stuffed my phone, wallet, power bank, cables, and Mojo gear inside, all without fishing around to find them. Add in the waterproof tech pocket, the stashable hi-vis rain layer, and that medical ID card, and you can tell this thing was engineered by people who actually ride out into the middle of nowhere.The polyester mesh panels help with airflow, but they aren’t enough on really hot, humid stretches. However, if you add in a super-soft lining and zero high-speed wind flap, and it’s a great place to spend the day. Still, at roughly 3.1 kg, it’s a heavy beast that drags on your shoulders by sundown. You trade weight for protection, but I’d love to see a slightly leaner version down the line.Nirvik Riding Trousers: The best part of the kitIf I had to choose one piece, it would be the trousers. I’ve worn riding pants before that tugged at the knees and crotch every time I moved. Getting on and off the bike was a chore. These were nothing like that.What it offers: The trousers come with CE Level 2 protectors at the knees and hips, with 600D polyester reinforcement at the critical zones. The pre-curved fit, along with an anti-tear Ripstop stretch panel at the crotch, is what makes them so easy to move in.That design does its job. I could sit, stand on the pegs or walk around at a halt, and I never felt cramped. Over several hours each day, that kind of comfort adds up. The armour stays where it should and doesn’t bother you, and I never had to stop to adjust a protector.Fit is adjustable, too. There are Velcro tabs at the waist, back of the knee and hem, so you can tweak things to your needs. I found that useful on colder mornings when I wore extra layers underneath, and again later in the day when it warmed up and I peeled a few off.These trousers are surprisingly light at 1.1 kg, and they smash down small in your luggage. You get four front pockets that are actually useful for stashing gear on the move, plus night-time reflective bits and matching trim that ties in nicely with the Nirvik jacket. Cleaning them was simple. For what they offer, you get a good balance of protection, comfort and everyday use.Royal Enfield Wanderer Boots: Solid and dependableThe Wanderer shoes tie the set together. They’re made from genuine leather and feel sturdy from the moment you put them on. They look good, too, and they don’t scream “riding boots” when you walk into a dhaba or a hotel. Well, that's for the optics. On the flip side, walking around off the bike isn’t the most comfortable, as the sole is built for riding.What it offers: The shoes are CE certified and built for cruising and adventure riding, with the same summer, winter and rain rating as the rest of the range. Plus, being made of genuine leather, they have a substantial feel as well.Love the fast-clip closures on these. When you’re gearing up in the freezing cold or stopping every ten minutes, they save you a ton of hassle. Your ankles feel totally locked in. At around 2.1 kg a pair, they’ve got some heft, but that’s just solid leather doing its job. Expect a couple of days of break-in stiffness before they mold to your feet, but once they do, they’re very comfortable. And when you’re caked in trail dust, a ten-second wipe clears it right off.VerdictHaving run the Nirvik jacket, pants, and those Wanderer boots all the way through the Himalayas, I’ve got plenty of respect for this gear. The jacket is bombproof and super practical, even if it feels a little heavy by the end of the day. The trousers were my personal favorite: super flexible and easy to live with. And the boots round off the setup nicely with solid, dependable support.This wasn't a cozy press launch with polished bikes and photo ops. This gear took a beating across terrain and unpredictable weather. Sure, there’s room to refine the jacket’s weight, but for real-world touring or even adventure riding, this kit punches way above its weight class.

articles.title: Italy tightens security as students, unions launch nationwide protests
articles.summary: Rallies across the country target living costs, investment in education and the wars in the Middle East.
articles.body:
Italy has tightened security as tens of thousands of students and unions took to the streets across the country.

Marches were held in dozens of cities nationwide on Friday. Rome, Milan and Naples were among those affected by the protests, which targeted soaring living costs , demanded investment in education and called for an end to the wars in the Middle East.

A large police presence was on hand, as the hard-right government tightened security measures in a bid to control potential unrest seen in Italy and other European states in recent weeks.

In Rome, security was stepped up around the Colosseum, Italy’s most visited tourist attraction, while Milan’s cathedral also received special protection.

A few skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of a protest in Turin, with other rallies in Bologna and Genoa.

The USB trade union called for a general strike that attracted large numbers of demonstrators, including truck drivers, taxi drivers and farmers. Rallies in recent weeks have demanded an end to higher fuel prices and rising defence spending.

Unions have also issued a joint call with peers in France, Greece, Spain, Turkiye and Morocco to demand an end to the wars in the Middle East, including the war in Gaza and “an end to the militarisation of ports”.

“Ports must not be used for the transport of weapons, ammunition, military equipment and troops,” the statement said. “Dockworkers do not work for war!”

The government last week agreed on a 175 million euro ($195 million) aid package for truck drivers, farmers and fishermen hit by soaring fuel prices linked to the war in the Middle East.

The prices paid in Italy for food, energy, transport and bills have risen by 68 percent since 2000, while the average wage fell by almost 5 percent.

Measures to support young people and families – such as an annual bonus of 2,500 euros for workers under 30 – have also been inserted into the draft 2027 budget currently being discussed among the various governing parties.

“I hope this can provide answers for young people in general… who feel that the state doesn’t care about them,” Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said at a news conference on Wednesday, stressing that the measures were “not for those who smash windows”.

Following clashes over the weekend of October 17-18 between youth and police in Milan, in which groups of mainly young people looted shops and smashed windows, Meloni toughened laws on public gatherings and eased restrictions on the detention of minors.
