articles.title: Major anti-government protests sweep across Italy
articles.summary: Farmers dumped manure on the streets of Turin on Friday as mass demonstrations unfurled across more than 50 cities in Italy.
articles.body: Farmers dumped manure on the streets of Turin on Friday as mass demonstrations unfurled across more than 50 cities in Italy. Fired up by a wave of similar protests elsewhere in Europe, tens of thousands of Italians took to the streets to protest soaring living costs and the poor state of public services such as healthcare and education. Friday’s nationwide action was spearheaded by the anti-capitalist trade union Unione Sindacale di Base (USB), and included workers across the public and private sectors. Transport workers had been slated to join the pickets too, but abandoned plans after Transport Minister Matteo Salvini threatened the sector with sanctions. The USB urged taxi drivers to go ahead with strikes, despite them receiving a similar warning. The largest rallies took place in Milan, Turin and the capital of Rome, where young and old united to vent their anger at Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her right-wing government. Demonstrators in Milan held placards bearing anti-government slogans, “Let’s oust the Meloni government—rebellion is just,” one read. In Naples, some protesters burnt photos of Meloni. Italy’s Interior Ministry said “preventative” arrests were made ahead of the marches to quell violence. Apart from a few isolated skirmishes, the demonstrations were largely peaceful as they continued into the afternoon. When some youngsters in Rome tried to set a dumpster on fire, others quickly extinguished the blaze, keen to avoid the type of violence that has marred similar protests in France. A strong anti-war sentiment was in evidence, with many protesters waving Palestinian flags as they marched. Others held banners opposing the government’s military spending. While Friday’s industrial action has been nationwide, demands have varied from one location to the next. In the northern city of Genoa, dockworkers mobilized against the “militarization” of the port in a bid to block the export of Italian-made arm shipments to conflict zones, including Israel. But in nearby Bologna, students called on the government to review education policy. Protests have swept through Europe in recent weeks as hundreds of thousands of people have demanded government action to ease the rising cost of living. Demonstrations in France began in late September with teachers and students protesting a lack of investment in education and woeful working conditions. The protests have since escalated to reflect wider cost-of-living concerns . A deepening housing crisis has triggered demonstrations across Spain and Portugal, with activists erecting encampments in the capitals’ central plazas. Albania has seen a series of anti-government protests, with thousands taking to the streets to highlight alleged government corruption and to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. And in Serbia, youth protests were effective in ousting long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić last weekend.

articles.title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said “AISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bonds”, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said “AISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bonds”, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" had brought to the fore. Neha’s refusal to sign the peace bond before a special executive magistrate and her subsequent challenge to the police move drew an obvious parallel. Did the CJP leaders - Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das - give in to peace bond pressure easily?“Peace bonds are being weaponised to curb democratic protests. Signing such peace bonds is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” the AISA national president said and claimed that she was detained within 10 minutes of protesting at Mandi House on October 16 and was told that she and other protesters were in breach of peace.“On one side, the Constitution gives us the right to dissent. On the other hand, such peace bonds are invoked only to detain people in the name of breach of peace. Therefore, signing such peace bonds is a principally wrong decision for us. It is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” Bora said defending her decision.Bora has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents in peace-bond proceedings. This, after she insisted for all documents relied upon in the show-cause notice seeking execution of her peace bond.Now, let’s rewind to October 10.The CJP’s call for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 had, as expected, evoked great national interest and anticipation. All eyes were on Abhijeet Dipke and his associates Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had in June-July this year led a successful youth mobilisation against NEET paper leak. The CJP-led protests had ensured that Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign as Union education minister. After all, they were the new heroes of GenZ, who had left the politicians far behind.But ahead of October 10, the national capital saw an unprecedented clampdown. The Delhi Police closed down anything and everything that could facilitate the movement of protesters to Jantar Mantar. For the CJP leadership, the message was loud and clear - they will not get a free passage, unlike in June when they were allowed to gather and mobilise youth at Jantar Mantar for their protests against NEET paper leak.But October 10 morning started with an anticlimax. The top 3 CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das travelled together from Mumbai to Delhi and were detained from aircraft as soon as they landed in the national capital. Thousands of protesters who had responded to their calls, braved the police clampdown. They were all detained.The CJP leaders were released a day later after giving an undertaking to maintain public order. Delhi Police said a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for maintaining peace and good behaviour for one year, following their preventive arrest on October 10.The CJP leaders made two more attempts to reclaim the streets - when Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka tried to reach Jantar Mantar and again when Dipke urged people to join the "Lehra Do Tiranga" march with the national flag at Central Park in Connaught Place.However, they were detained again and made to sign peace bonds to come out of detention. And while the CJP leaders failed to recreate the magic of Jantar Mantar 1.0, AISA leader Neha Bora took the centrestage. The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. However, every time she was released, she would come back to the streets and continue with her protests.During the peak of the protests, Neha Bora hogged the headlines for foxing the police. On October 11, Neha Bora announced a gathering at RK Ashram Marg Metro Station around 2:30pm as part of demonstrations heading toward central Delhi and Jantar Mantar.Heavy police deployment and barricades were set up around RK Ashram Marg to prevent demonstrators from moving toward Jantar Mantar. During the confrontation, police mistakenly chased and detained another protester whose face was partially covered, believing her to be Neha Bora.While police attention was focused at RK Ashram Marg, Neha Bora surfaced near Connaught Place (CP), breaching barricades and running alongside fellow demonstrators in a dash that went viral on social media.Little wonder then, when a user on X called Neha Bora "more talented" than CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and described her as a "complete GenZ icon", Dipke responded simply: "I agree." The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete GenZ icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura.” It was a comparison that manifested all along the “vote chori” protests.Neha Bora was on the streets every time she was released from detention by the police. She was everywhere - with the CJP leadership, the social activists and also the politicians. When Rahul Gandhi chose to walk behind her during one of the protest marches of INDIA bloc, it spoke volumes about the impact she had made with her street politics. Clearly, the campaign against “vote chori” had put the spotlight on Neha Bora, even as the CJP struggled to find their way to the centre stage of the protests.For the CJP, it was a harsh realisation that a lot had changed between July and October. Unlike the anti-NEET paper leak protests in June-July, the Congress-led INDIA bloc this time around were already on the streets demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Interestingly, while the INDIA bloc’s original protest schedule had only one announced street protest on October 6, the group returned back to the streets four days in a row till October 9, which was a day before the announced CJP protest.The CJP and the Congress had stayed away from each other during the anti-NEET protests. After Jantar Mantar 1.0 was over, the 'cockroaches' carried out their own campaigns in different states, while the Congress shifted focus to protests against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Abhijeet Dipke has announced that he has no political plans and would prefer to keep CJP as a pressure group. So when CJP announced support for INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, it set tongues wagging about their political ambitions.With CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 not shaping out as they would have hoped, perhaps its leadership should take a leaf out of Saurav Das’s advice on X to a Congress “soldier” who had questioned why youth Congress and NSUI activists were being detained as soon as they hit the streets and cockroaches were allowed to roam free. Responding to him, CJP co-founder Saurav Das had then said: “if u guys r detained immediately, then u must rethink ur strategy. don’t blame others for ur failures.”The context of that remark was different and CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 campaign was in no way a failure, but Sourav's take on “rethinking strategy” perhaps holds true for the cockroaches at present.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
articles.summary: It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.
articles.body:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has released her first public statement since her botched execution in September.

"There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said in the statement.

"My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul."

Pike, 50, was discharged from hospital at the end of last month after surviving two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital, which left her in a critical condition.

She has since been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

Pike is thought to be the only person to survive an execution attempt by lethal injection.

I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's

I interviewed Christa Pike 20 years ago - I can't stop thinking about her

What happened in Christa Pike's failed US execution, and how did she survive?

"I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger," she said in her statement on Friday. "But healing is not the same as being okay."

Her lawyers previously said she had suffered from pneumonia following the attempted execution, had significant swelling on her arms and was also unable to swallow.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.

Shipp was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.

Pike's botched execution captivated and shocked the world last month and shocked Pike, too.

"I had not contemplated life beyond that night, and I'm deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position," she said in her statement.

Bethany Mann, a friend of Pike's and a founder of Child Arise Tennessee, which supports children and families affected by parental incarceration, told the BBC on Friday that she had been in direct contact with Pike since the botched execution attempt.

When asked about her reaction to Pike's statement, Mann said: "Truthfully, I don't know that I have anything to add to what Christa has already expressed so powerfully herself, and I want to be respectful of her privacy."

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the remainder of the year and ordered an independent review to "determine exactly what occurred".

Lee was asked by reporters this week about a potential second execution attempt. "I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts," he responded.

Speaking about the state's response to what happened to Pike, Mann said: "I find it deeply troubling that, even after what Christa endured, Governor Lee has shown little public willingness to reconsider the death penalty itself, rather than simply the procedures used to carry it out."

She added: "What happened to Christa is not an isolated tragedy, nor should this conversation begin and end with her."

The Tennessee Department of Correction has not explained why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used.

It declined comment on Pike's statement when contacted by the BBC.

Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death and attended the botched execution, later calling it a "mess".

She told a local ABC News affiliate in Florida, where she lives, that she thinks the state owes her an apology.

"All I wanted was justice," Martinez said.

Pike was the first woman scheduled to be executed in the state of Tennessee in over 200 years.

Her lawyers have spent decades appealing her case. In the days leading up to her scheduled execution, both the US Supreme Court and Lee declined to block the execution.

The attempted execution of Pike was not the first in Tennessee in 2026 that did not go to plan.

The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein for a lethal injection. He was granted a year's reprieve by the governor.

In 2022, more than a third of executions across the US were botched or highly problematic, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, which does not take an ethical stance on the penalty.

articles.title: Ukraine invests in firepower as it inflicts a new Russian casualty record
articles.summary: Recent Starlink suspension did not much affect Ukrainian lethality, but Kyiv shows it is losing trust in the US.
articles.body:
Ukraine’s military says Russian casualties reached 49,040 in October – a new monthly record.

The General Staff’s estimate of dead and incapacitated Russian troops, as of October 28, comes close to fulfilling Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s goal set in January of at least 50,000 enemy casualties a month by the end of 2026.

Zelenskyy had said that was “a level of destruction of the occupier at which Russian losses exceed the number of reinforcements they can send.”

The previous monthly high of 46,230 was set in September, with both records marking a sharp increase in reported Russian dead and wounded since the summer.

Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert Brovdi called it a “massive industrial slaughter”.

Al Jazeera cannot independently verify casualty estimates by either side. Ukraine’s military says it has video documentation of each strike.

Aerial drones are responsible for most of the casualties Ukraine inflicts, and Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara this week asked his European allies for funding to double drone production next year to about 16 million units.

The goal, he said, was “to scale up joint production of Ukrainian drones in other countries”.

Zelenskyy has said Ukraine could even triple drone production given enough money. Ukraine has decided that mass is the key to winning the war against Russia in terms of firepower.

“We see signs that mass production is preferred over technological sophistication,” said Ukrainian Defence Ministry adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov. “Mass production and simplicity will overcome technology.”

On October 28, the Netherlands and UK took steps to help Ukraine achieve its goal.

The Netherlands said it would provide 500 million euros ($560m) in immediate additional military aid and 1.2 billion euros ($1.34bn) in additional financing.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham upped Britain’s commitments by 10 billion pounds ($13.4bn) over three years, of which 3 billion pounds ($4bn) will be for weapons.

Ukraine announced its Starlink satellite navigation services were back to normal on October 24. “Communication remains stable at speeds exceeding 400km/h,” said the Defence Ministry.

On October 14, Ukraine had reported it was losing control of its drones above about 150km/h (100mph), making it difficult to mount defence against Russian jet-powered drones travelling above 500km/h.

After initially denying involvement, Starlink owner Elon Musk said on October 24 that he had “closed a loophole” that had allowed Ukraine to use Starlink offensively.

But Ukraine appeared to be thinking beyond Starlink and its Pentagon-owned military-grade service, Starshield.

On October 22, Ukraine and Finland announced they were jointly developing an independent sovereign military satellite system. Poland-based ICEYE and Finnish Nokia said they were partnering to realise the system, which would begin to launch satellites in 2028.

Other Europeans may be interested. On October 28, Zelenskyy also discussed satellite technology collaboration with Dutch premier Rob Jetten.

Ukraine said while they lasted, Starlink’s speed restrictions damaged its interception of Russian jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones.

The Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, said the 10-day outage caused Ukraine’s interception rate to fall from 77 percent to 74 percent.

Yet the rate seemed to be improving regardless.

According to Ukrainian Air Force data, Ukraine managed to shoot down at least 75 percent of jet-powered drones during the week ending October 29.

That was far above the three-month average shoot-down rate of 60 percent for jet-powered drones, suggesting that Ukraine is adapting fast.

Still, many Russian drones are getting through. One struck a train platform in the central city of Dnipro on October 29 , killing at least 14 people.

Ukraine is also concerned that the US administration is hesitating about sending ballistic missile interceptors European allies have paid for.

“The artificial and prolonged delays in the delivery of interceptor missiles for Patriot and NASAMS systems, which unfortunately have been occurring recently, are directly helping Russia achieve the goals of its terrorist campaign,” Zelenskyy said, after Russian ballistics hit a university campus in downtown Kyiv on October 27.

The previous day, Khmara had asked European allies to transfer 10 percent of their existing stocks of interceptors as an advance on future orders.

Ukraine struck Russia during the past week, too.

On October 23, Ukrainian missiles destroyed the main microchip production building of Proton-Electrotex in the city of Orel, which makes missile components.

During the week, Ukraine damaged five chemical plants, NAK Azot, Toliattykauchuk, Omskiy Kauchuk, Energiya and Voronezhsintezkauchuk, which make solid rocket propellants used in missiles.

It also damaged the Voronezh Aircraft Company and VSMPO-AVISMA, two factories building airframes or the metals for them.

Ukraine has also been developing underground warfare, far from the battlefields monitored by drones, planes and satellites.

On October 22, its Khartiia Corps, originally a volunteer unit but now part of the National Guard, announced it had successfully completed an operation to flush Russian infiltrators out of a disused gas pipeline.

The Russians were using the pipeline to move troops from occupied parts of Kharkiv to the front line city of Kupiansk.

“The Russians tried to use underground gas pipelines to move past our positions. Our warriors turned this tactic against the Russians and used this system of underground pipelines against the occupiers with extraordinary success,” said Zelenskyy.

Ukraine’s Operation Veles advanced 15km (10 miles) underground through the pipeline and tunnels to emerge behind Russian positions, said Brigadier General Ihor Oboloenskyi.

Khartiia Corps said it coordinated underground attacks from pipes and tunnels with overland attacks and drones to surprise the enemy from several different directions at once, killing or wounding 100 Russian soldiers and capturing 30.

Russian forces had used the pipelines to evacuate their wounded, too, and were filmed marching Ukrainian civilians among them as human shields, said Viktor Tregubov, United Forces Group spokesman.

Ukraine’s forces besieged the Russians inside the pipeline, said Vladimir Dektyarev, an officer of Khartiia Corps. “Even after they were surrounded, they sat for over a month, until their food ran out, waiting for a command from their command for permission to surrender.”

Veles marked the third operation this year where Ukrainian forces have pushed Russian forces back and reclaimed land.

In the south of the country, too, Ukrainian forces were reported to have liberated three settlements – Peredubova, Komar and Fedorivka – on the Donetsk-Zaporizhia border, expanding an area of reclaimed territory there.

Although the US is still on track to bring Ukrainian and Russian technical teams to the negotiating table on November 10, and Zelenskyy supported a ceasefire on energy infrastructure and grain exports, Russia downplayed expectations.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke of Ukraine as “the territory of historical Russia” on October 22, denying the existence of a Ukrainian people and refusing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure.

His foreign policy adviser, Valery Ushakov, said the talks “will not resolve much”.

When Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb held a call with Putin on October 27 – their first contact with him since assuming office – Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov dismissed the conversation as “Europeans’ desire to squeeze into the negotiation process.”

articles.title: Visit Norway makes toilets ‘great again’ after Trump’s ‘sh*t house country’ jab
articles.summary: Norway’s tourism board has launched a tongue-in-cheek toilet campaign to show off the country’s most scenic restrooms after US President Donald Trump branded the Nordic nation a “sh*t house country.”
articles.body: Norway’s tourism board has launched a tongue-in-cheek toilet campaign to show off the country’s most scenic restrooms after US President Donald Trump branded the Nordic nation a “sh*t house country.” Trump delivered his scathing comments on the campaign trail, days before voters head to the polls for the midterm elections. He said on Sunday that he would welcome immigrants to the US from some countries, but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize … ​So I don’t want anybody from Norway.” Trump later said at the same rally: “Norway has become a sh*t house country, actually.” Now, Visit Norway has embraced the label, asking, “Are these the world’s best sh*t houses?” in an article online that showcases the facilities available in the scenic Scandinavian nation. Highlighting its campaign on social media this week, the tourist board posted several of the images and wrote: “So, we heard some noise about ‘s…house country’… What can we say, we do have some of the world’s most beautiful and spectacular toilets.” The Norwegian marketing campaign shows photos and footage of some of the glorious facilities, accompanied by captions such as: “Norway makes sh*thouses great again! These toilets are worth a visit, both when you really have to go – and when you don’t.” Among the featured bathrooms is that at the Stegastein viewpoint in the Sognefjord region, which the tourist board said has been described as one of the world’s 10 best public toilets by DesignCurial. It also highlights the wave-shaped Ureddplassen on the Helgeland coast. Described on the site as “architectural masterpieces,” the featured restrooms include a golden one on the island Senja, as well as one that runs on solar power in the Sognefjord area. Promising “more to come” with regards to restrooms being built to impress, the website concludes: “Norway’s portfolio of spectacular toilets is, as you can see, filled with great examples of how something as boring as a loo can become a tourist attraction.” The US President has also called Haiti, ​Libya, Somalia and Yemen “sh*t house countries.” But his attack on Norway seems to have stemmed from losing out on the Nobel Peace Prize, which was awarded to South African human rights pioneer Navi Pillay earlier this month. Trump has repeatedly been reminded by the Norwegians that the prize is awarded by an independent Nobel Committee and not the government of Norway.

articles.title: Bhutan hot springs hit by flood from glacial lake burst
articles.summary: No injuries reported after glacial lake burst, causing a flash flood and disrupting Bhutan’s Gasa Tshachu hot springs.
articles.body:
A flood caused by the Shintaphu glacial lake bursting its banks has washed away infrastructure at the Gasa Tshachu natural hot springs in the Himalayan ⁠kingdom of Bhutan.

According to state broadcaster BBS on Friday, no injuries or loss of life had been reported from Thursday night’s flash flood.

It added that the extent of the damage was unknown because of “darkness and the strong flow” of floodwaters.

Two Bailey bridges, which are bridges built in portable, prefabricated sections, may also have been washed away, BBS said.

According to Kuensel, Bhutan’s national newspaper, part of the road leading to the village of Laya, where the springs are located, had also been washed away, rendering it impassable. It added that the road has been closed to traffic indefinitely.

Kuensel said that as authorities assess the damage, concerns have emerged about a large artificial lake formed after the flood-affected river channels conjoined following the outburst.

Residents along the Mochhu and Punatsangchhu river valleys were also advised to remain vigilant and avoid riverbanks and flood-prone areas, the report added.

Moreover, in neighbouring India, flood warnings were issued in parts of West Bengal and Assam following the glacial lake outburst, India’s NDTV broadcaster reported.

The hot springs at Gasa Tshachu are a major tourist attraction in the northern part of Bhutan, nestled between India and China.

They were also hit by a flash flood in 2021 when the Mochhu River changed course and swept through the area.

In neighbouring Nepal , a mountainous area about 600km (380 miles) to the west, a flash flood on its border with China in August killed more than 1,500 people and left more than 5,000 missing.

articles.title: Netanyahu's bloc falls short as longtime allies reportedly weigh move that could end his rule
articles.summary: Netanyahu's bloc secured only 53 Knesset seats as ultra-Orthodox allies reportedly explore breaking ranks to back Gadi Eisenkot's opposition.
articles.body: Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors. The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position. Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results. ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals. A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation. The source said opposition leaders are approaching coalition negotiations with patience and experience rather than treating the inconclusive results as a defeat, arguing that the next government could depend on their ability to forge partnerships that previously seemed unlikely. FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER Ultra-Orthodox allies explore a break with Netanyahu In a potentially significant development Friday, Israeli journalist Yishai Cohen of Kikar HaShabbat reported that Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading ultra-Orthodox religious authority, had instructed lawmakers from Degel HaTorah, part of United Torah Judaism, to open discussions with the opposition. According to the report, the objective is to reach an arrangement protecting the status of yeshiva students amid the longstanding dispute over mandatory military service. Channel 12 reported that figures within the ultra-Orthodox party were considering allowing an Eisenkot-led minority government to survive through outside parliamentary support, potentially breaking with Netanyahu. "Our votes are not in Netanyahu's pocket," party figures told Channel 12, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language report. However, the office of United Torah Judaism Chairman Yaakov Asher denied that any instruction to begin negotiations had been issued. Such an arrangement would represent a significant shift from the party's longstanding alliance with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's pledge to expand military conscription among ultra-Orthodox men remains a major obstacle, although Channel 12 reported that party figures were willing to consider a compromise on the issue. The source familiar with opposition discussions told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot's camp had been preparing for the possibility of cooperation with ultra-Orthodox parties well before the election, suggesting that some of the options now being discussed had already been under consideration behind the scenes. According to the source, such an arrangement could require compromises over military service and potentially outside parliamentary support from Arab lawmakers, bringing together political factions whose positions appeared irreconcilable during the campaign. FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE Arab parties signal flexibility, but obstacles remain Another possibility rests with the Arab parties, which nearly doubled their parliamentary representation from 10 to 19 seats following a surge in turnout. But the prospects of an Arab-backed government have drawn conflicting assessments. Channel 12 reported Thursday that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas had expressed deep skepticism about the possibility of establishing an Eisenkot-led minority government supported by Arab lawmakers. Israeli political commentator Amit Segal also argued that the available options had narrowed considerably, identifying a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government or another election as the two principal remaining possibilities. Mohammed Majadla, head of the news division at Radio Nas and a Channel 12 political commentator, offered a different assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital, arguing that both Ra'am and the Joint List were prepared to use their parliamentary influence to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power. "The two Arab lists agree on two things," Majadla said in the Hebrew-language interview. "First, they are prepared to do everything within the political process to ensure Netanyahu does not return to power." According to Majadla, that could include joining a coalition, providing outside parliamentary support or abstaining from key votes. He said their second shared priority was avoiding another election, which Arab political leaders fear could reverse their gains. "The ball is now in Eisenkot's court, not in the Arab parties' court," Majadla said. "As far as the Arab parties are concerned, I can tell you they are truly prepared to do everything to make this happen." Majadla suggested that public declarations should not necessarily be treated as final positions, particularly as parties seek leverage during coalition negotiations. The difficulties extend beyond the Arab parties. Eisenkot's potential partners include politicians who strongly oppose cooperation with ultra-Orthodox factions, while several opposition leaders campaigned against relying on Arab lawmakers to govern. NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING Unity government or another election? A national unity government involving Likud and Yashar would offer a more straightforward mathematical route to a majority, but would require Eisenkot to reconsider his campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government. For Netanyahu, the lengthy coalition formation process could provide additional opportunities. If Eisenkot receives the mandate to form a government but fails, President Isaac Herzog could assign the task to another candidate, potentially giving Netanyahu another chance to assemble a coalition. If successive efforts fail, Israel could face another election. Despite the obstacles, the source familiar with opposition discussions pointed to Bennett and Lapid's experience navigating complex coalition negotiations as an important asset. "They've both played this game many times. They know it, and they're not rattled," the source said, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language conversation. The source suggested that Bennett's experience working with Netanyahu gives him a particular understanding of the prime minister's negotiating tactics, while Lapid brings additional experience in coalition-building. Former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, one of the opposition's senior figures, acknowledged Friday that forming a government would be considerably more difficult than campaigning against Netanyahu. "Now comes the truly hard part: trying to form a government," Lapid wrote on X, urging supporters to remain patient. "It takes place in small rooms, slowly, away from the cameras," he wrote, according to a translation of his Hebrew-language statement, emphasizing the importance of negotiations conducted out of public view. The negotiations will also unfold against the backdrop of the Trump administration's Middle East agenda. The source familiar with opposition discussions said understanding Washington's regional priorities could become an important consideration in shaping a future government, although no specific American role in coalition negotiations has been confirmed. The election results are scheduled to be formally submitted to President Herzog on November 4, following remaining verification procedures. The new Knesset is expected to be sworn in November 10. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For now, the election has settled the question of how Israelis voted, but not who will govern them. A source familiar with the negotiations concluded: "Whoever manages to forge new partnerships will move forward. Whoever doesn't will remain stuck."

articles.title: Hampshire parents fined for employing teen son in family food trailer
articles.summary: Dexter's parents are ordered to pay £7,200 after admitting to breaking council byelaws.
articles.body:
The parents of a 14-year-old boy have been fined for allowing him to work on the family's mobile food trailer.

Karen and Greg Olejarka pleaded guilty at Southampton Magistrates' Court to breaching Hampshire County Council's byelaws prohibiting under-16s from working in commercial kitchens.

The Hampshire couple have been fined £600 each and ordered to pay a further £6,000 in costs.

The family had argued they were supporting their son Dexter's passion for cooking by allowing him to prepare food in the trailer from the age of 12.

District Judge Anthony Callaway said it was significant that Dexter was seen using deep fat fryers, knives and working in a commercial kitchen run for profit.

The family had argued the food trailer should not be regarded as a commercial kitchen, and insisted that Dexter's education was not affected.

Greg Olejarka said: "No one considered Dexter in all of this. They prosecute us as parents for supporting our child to become someone with skills."

Hampshire County Council became aware of Dexter after a YouTube video praising the teenager's cooking skills showed him using a grill and a deep fat fryer.

Teen chef pleads to be allowed to keep cooking

Banned teen chef helps foodbank celebrate anniversary

The family said they were tackling the dispute with the council while supporting another son, while he received treatment for blood cancer.

Karen Olejarka said they pleaded guilty as fighting the case would have been too expensive.

"We've gone from fighting for our second son to be able to live his life, to fighting for our oldest son to live," she said.

At an earlier hearing, Hampshire County Council said it had attempted to resolve the issue before prosecution, but prosecutor Ian Jenkins said Dexter's father had "gone nuclear" and made it a national issue.

Child employment in England is covered by the Children and Young Person Act 1933, and also by local byelaws drawn up by each local authority.

While Hampshire's byelaws state that "children may do light work from the age of 13 years until they are no longer of compulsory school age", employment in commercial kitchens is prohibited until the age of 16.

The council said: "We will only consider legal action in the most exceptional circumstances, where there are safeguarding concerns that cannot be addressed in other ways.

"The defendants in this case pleaded guilty and they appear to have recognised that the employment of Dexter in a commercial kitchen was unlawful."

Dexter's parents said he was no longer helping out on the food trailer.

articles.title: Ethnic cleansing fears rise as Israel squeezes space in Gaza: UN
articles.summary: Israeli forces are treating the ‘Yellow Line’, which is encroaching westward, as ‘a kill zone’, the OHCHR says.
articles.body:
Israeli forces in Gaza are displacing more Palestinians and their actions continue to raise concerns of ethnic cleansing, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) has warned.

Palestinians are being repeatedly displaced by Israeli forces into a decreasing fraction of the besieged enclave, an OHCHR statement issued on Friday said.

The Israeli army is further encroaching on areas past its deployment line, also known as the “Yellow Line,” and “Israeli forces appear to treat the yellow line as a kill zone,” preventing Palestinians from returning to what is left of their homes on the other side, the UN agency said.

The OHCHR cautioned that the Israeli military is destroying remaining civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, as it continues its stated aim of increasing its military deployment area to 70 percent of Gaza’s territory.

Human rights groups and aid agencies have repeatedly called on Israel to stop forcibly displacing Palestinians in Gaza and attacking shelters throughout the conflict.

The OHCHR documented the westward expansion of the Israeli military over the past two weeks, triggering new displacement of Palestinians in Shujayea, Gaza City, and in eastern Bureij, eastern Deir el-Balah and eastern al-Maghazi in Central Gaza.

The UN agency noted that in Shujayea, at least two Israeli attacks were reported on displacement camps, with explosive robots detonating the few buildings left standing in the area.

The OHCHR also said that it received reports that an Israeli drone dropped munitions on a tent housing displaced Palestinians at the Shujayea junction on Sunday. The Palestinian Ministry of Public Works and Housing in Gaza said the resulting fire displaced 200 families comprising 800 people.

Ajith Sunghay, head of the OHCHR in occupied Palestine, said the “nightmare of displacement” in Gaza was both “acute and chronic”.

“Those displaced before the announcement of a ceasefire have little to no prospect of return to the areas they fled, most of which are inaccessible because they fall beyond the so-called Yellow Line. And they continue to be displaced again and again.”

Despite an ongoing ceasefire , Israeli attacks on Gaza have continued, with at least 1,574 people killed and 5,687 others wounded since the agreement came into place on October 11, 2025, according to the enclave’s Ministry of Health.

Since the genocidal war began in October 2023, Israeli attacks have killed at least 74,570 people and wounded 175,808 others.

articles.title: Travel influencer, 24, killed after pickup truck is swept away in terrifying river crossing
articles.summary: Influencer Emma Marie Laurent of France was among three women killed when a pickup truck was swept away crossing Nicaragua's Nahualapa River after heavy rainfall.
articles.body: A 24-year-old travel influencer was killed after a pickup truck carrying a group of travelers was swept away while crossing a river in Nicaragua. French traveler Emma Marie Laurent was one of three women who died after the vehicle was caught in strong currents following heavy rainfall, according to news agency Jam Press. The group was traveling through El Manzano, a community in the northwestern department of Chinandega, when they attempted to cross the Nahualapa River at around 1 a.m. on Oct. 9, the same source reported. AMERICAN TOURIST FALLS 1,000 FEET TO HER DEATH WHILE CHASING PERFECT MOUNTAIN PHOTO Recent rainfall had caused the river to rise, creating dangerous conditions before the vehicle attempted to cross. The driver, identified as Mexican national Martin Gerardo García Girón, reportedly stepped out of the pickup to assess the water level before attempting the crossing, according to Jam Press. The water reportedly came close to the driver's knees, but the current swept the pickup away and caused it to overturn. The driver survived, though accounts have differed on whether other passengers also made it to safety, according to Jam Press. Authorities were investigating the circumstances surrounding the crossing. "This is a tragedy," Murillo said, according to reports. "We express our solidarity and our call to remain vigilant and, in the face of such tragedies, to express our full solidarity." Murillo also warned about the dangers of crossing rivers during Nicaragua's rainy season. "Rivers are deceptive; one thinks they are calm and, suddenly, the current comes, and we have tragedies like this that bring mourning to families," she said, according to Jam Press. Laurent had developed an online following by sharing her travels around the world, including glimpses of life on the road from her van. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ She described herself as "your barefoot BFF" on Instagram, where she had nearly 43,000 followers at the time of her death, Jam Press reported. Laurent appeared to have shared her final social media post on Oct. 2, uploading a video from a recent trip to Portugal. In the post, she reflected on the importance of appreciating everyday moments. articles.title: Massachusetts police capture New Hampshire fugitive who’d been on lam for nearly a year
articles.summary: A New Hampshire fugitive who had been on the run for almost a year was captured in neighboring Massachusetts this week after one last frantic attempt to evade police, law enforcement agencies said.
articles.body: A New Hampshire fugitive who had been on the run for almost a year was captured in neighboring Massachusetts this week after one last frantic attempt to evade police, law enforcement agencies said. Daquhan Cromer, 29, was taken into custody shortly after noon Wednesday in Lowell, a day after he dodged police in Salem, New Hampshire on Tuesday night, officials said. Cromer was “wanted on an escape warrant from New Hampshire State Prison and in connection with multiple felonies in Salem,” authorities in that New Hampshire town said. His flight prompted a shelter-in-place order in Salem night on Tuesday night, which was lifted by Wednesday morning. He was surrounded by police almost 15 miles away in Lowell, where he surrendered without incident, officials said. “Through different investigative methods, they were able to track him down to a residence,” Salem police Lt. Robert Kirley told reporters. “And once they got to that residence, they were looking for him and he was inside.” Cromer had fled a halfway house in Manchester, New Hampshire, in December 2025, NBC Boston reported.

articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
articles.summary: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
articles.body:
Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).

Shares in Intel plummeted by as much as 30% on Friday, following Google owner Alphabet's stock price plunging by more than $500bn (£374bn) in the previous day's trading.

Other tech stocks including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, sank more than 3.5%.

While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.

Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800.6bn between them in 2026.

Alphabet's stock market value plunged on Thursday after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.

Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 2.2% after Thursday's slide of more than 12%.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value as its shares continued to fall in Friday trading.

The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

Amazon shares fell as far as 6% in overnight trading after the company's reported earnings fell short of investors' expectations.

Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months.

The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers.

Shares recovered slightly from the overnight fall but were still down about 1.6% in Friday trading.

Reddit stock was down by 26%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.

Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by nearly 20%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.

Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.

Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.

He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".

"The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down."

Many analysts have been debating the possibility of an AI bubble in the stock market.

The worry is that some tech firms will not be able to justify their sky-high valuations because the cost of building AI data centres and developing the software will end up being greater than the money they can make from it.

Kathleen Brookes, research director at trading firm XTB, said there have been many ups and downs in AI trade in recent months.

"Investors have turned ruthless, punishing any signs of disappointment in [third quarter] earnings," she said.

"The AI trade has had a good run in recent years, but now investors want payback, and companies like Alphabet and Intel are in the crosshairs."

However, stock market values for many of these companies remain well above where they were a year ago.

While the Nasdaq is down 3.5% in Friday trading, it is up 7.6% over the last year. Similarly Amazon is up nearly 7% over the past 12 months, while Alphabet is down 1.6%.

Brookes noted that November is typically a strong month for stocks.

"If we see AI stocks continue to struggle in the coming days, it could suggest the AI trade is past its peak, and investors will be looking for a new theme to drive markets," she said.

articles.title: ICE officer is indicted after striking, injuring immigrant with his vehicle in Houston
articles.summary: A Texas grand jury indicted ICE agent Mario Alberto Morales on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
articles.body: A Texas grand jury indicted ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales Friday on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, alleging he drove his vehicle into Miguel Parra Hernandez, who was on foot, earlier this month, the Harris County District Attorney’s Office said Friday. The indictment of Morales, 33, was handed up by a Harris County grand jury Friday morning. The indictment is the first of an immigration agent in Texas. ICE enforcement officer Christian Castro was charged in the January shooting of Julio Sosa-Celis in Minnesota. “The evidence that we have in this case is as clear as any that I’ve ever prosecuted or investigated,” Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said in a news conference Friday. At the news conference, Teare played body camera video from an officer that showed the officer snapping the steering wheel left and seconds later a wail can immediately be heard. Parra is on the ground with his face on the pavement and the officer turns him over. “You ran over me,” Parra cries. The officer, who is standing over Parra who continues wailing in agony, the video shows. The officer tells him “You got hit with the car, bro.” The officer turns him over and tries to pick Parra up from his shoulders, but Parra cries out louder. The officer is heard saying, “I was coming in and I hit him with the car.” He suggests trying to put Parra in the car. “An ICE badge does not give you free rein to injure, kill, or violate the constitutional rights of anyone,” Teare said. The Oct. 10 collision left Parra with hip, leg and ankle injuries, including a broken leg, according to his family and representatives. Parra is at a rehab facility under ICE custody, Teare said. In a statement issued after the collision, ICE said Parra “ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck.” The agent was driving an SUV. But after reviewing video collected by investigators in his office from local businesses and bystanders, Teare accused the agent of deliberately running over Parra. ICE has previously said accusations that its agent intentionally struck Parra were “reckless” and “false.” In an emailed statement shortly after the indictment was announced, an ICE spokesperson said the indictment “is nothing more than a political stunt by Houston sanctuary politicians.” The spokesperson stated that only federal agencies can investigate “federal officers acting in the course of their duties,” and that local governments don’t have the authority to run such an investigation. Teare, a Democrat, said at the press conference that it’s “false” that they can’t investigate. ICE repeated its view that that allegations that the ICE officer struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are “reckless” and “false.” DHS placed an officer on administrative leave after the collision, a senior DHS official told NBC News earlier this month. Security video of the incident obtained by NBC affiliate KPRC of Houston shows a white truck facing the opposite direction of traffic on a busy roadway. Parra and another man exit the white truck and run, the video shows. At about the same time, the video shows, another vehicle jumps a yellow median and heads in Parra’s direction. The video then shows the vehicle, which is not marked, swerving left toward Parra’s path, in front of a truck stopped in a shopping center. When the parked truck leaves, a man can be seen lying on the pavement behind the ICE vehicle, the video shows. Teare, who worked several years as a Harris County vehicle crimes division chief, had previously told NBC News that he had sought critical data from the vehicle involved in the collision but ICE moved the car from the scene. Parra has lived in the U.S. for 34 years, having arrived at age 14, and he has no criminal record, his attorney told NBC News. He had been doing stucco work when he was struck, according to an advocate. DHS said he was in the country without legal permission. ICE had said it was conducting a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes and was not targeting Parra or another man who was also in a truck with Mendoza-Cervantes before they fled on foot. But Mendoza-Cervantes’ daughter told Houston immigrant rights group FIEL of Houston and Parra’s attorney Kim Bruno that her father had been dead since 2017.

articles.title: The US should strongly advocate for political prisoner releases, global freedom
articles.summary: While celebrating recent political prisoner releases, author Nicole Bibbins Sedaca argues that the United States must use sanctions and diplomatic pressure to challenge the systemic use of imprisonment by autocratic regimes.
articles.body:
It is a familiar picture. An emaciated political prisoner walks off a plane, greeted by family and strangers stunned to see this person in the flesh. On the former captive’s face flash emotions of both incomprehensible relief and dizzying disbelief. These rare releases of political prisoners typically follow the tireless advocacy of family, friends, governments, and civil society.

As we celebrate these breakthrough moments of freedom, we should never forget the bigger picture that lurks behind each release, namely brutal autocratic regimes consolidating and asserting power by using human pawns and the capricious denial of freedom.

The United States should continue to advocate for the release of political prisoners, utilize tools to punish and deter such abuses, and — most importantly — recognize that any regime involved in political imprisonment lacks the values and trustworthiness for long-term American partnership.

We must naturally pursue short-term engagement with many nations to advance and protect American interests. We should also acknowledge, however, that the depravity of a regime denying freedom to its own citizens undermines that nation’s viability as a trusted partner. Those nations that share our democratic values are stronger, better, more sustainable partners.

We have celebrated the rare prisoner releases by name. Journalist Jason Rezian, freed from Iran. Pastor Ezra Jin , freed from China. Journalist Evan Gershkovich, freed from Russia. Activist Maryam Akbari Monfared, freed from Iran. Artist-turned-activist Luis Manuel Otero Alcantara , freed from Cuba. Pastor-turned-activist Evan Mawarire, freed from Zimbabwe.

Each release is unquestionably a welcome development, and at the George W. Bush Institute, we celebrate every individual who is restored to freedom. Yet each is a reminder of a growing tide of autocratic leaders, often loosely aligned with each other, willing to throw countless numbers of innocent people in prison, most often for practicing their faith, writing a news article, advocating for their rights, or demanding justice.

These autocratic leaders direct myriad government staff — from senior officials to the lowest prison guard — to deny these people their freedom, to harass their families and limit contact, to treat them with disdain and abuse, to deny access to medicine, adequate food, and fresh air, and — all too often — to subject them to inhuman abuse and torture. These are usually strategic, planned arrests designed not only to silence the individual but to send chills through the entire community.

All of this is because these individuals dared to worship, speak, assemble and associate, foundational freedoms we know well — and value deeply — in the United States.

Quite often, these regimes follow high-profile releases with the arrest of other activists or colleagues of the released person, a “replenishment” of political prisoners. And frequently they continue to harass the individual and their community long after the release has occurred. All too often, these individuals are forced from their home country permanently.

Each release is simply undoing a deeply unjust action that these rulers chose to do; it should be recognized as such, not as an act of charity.

Since Jin’s July release, at least seven Christian house churches have been raided. At least 150 pastors remain imprisoned, and eight Christians who were seized with Jin remain behind bars .

Since Otero Alcantara’s July release, at least a dozen more people have been incarcerated, according to Prisoners Defenders , a leading group tracking political imprisonment in Cuba. It estimates that Cuban jails held 1,339 political prisoners as of August, a number that has steadily increased over the course of the year.

The administration and members of Congress should expand their efforts to call for the release of political prisoners, especially those held by China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, authoritarian nations increasingly aligned in their interests.

American elected officials should continue to call for the release of individual prisoners by name: Wang Yi, Jimmy Lai , and Dr. Gulshan Abbas in China; Lev Schosberg in Russia; Narges Mohammadi in Iran.

This will serve as a powerful reminder that the U.S. stands for liberty and won’t turn a blind eye to repression by these regimes. It would also be an important boost for democracy defenders in each country, showing that they are not alone and that the democratic world stands with them.

Beyond individual case advocacy, the administration and U.S. Congress should use the powerful tools at their disposal, including sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act , to impose a real penalty on those involved with imprisoning innocent democracy activists.

Finally, the administration and Congress should calibrate relations accordingly with all nations that choose to use political imprisonment to silence freedom defenders.

Each person reunited with their loved ones is a reason to rejoice. But let us honor their stories, struggles and aspirations by focusing on the bigger fight against autocratic regimes and to show them that we won’t allow the normalization of their dehumanizing practice of political imprisonment.

Nicole Bibbins Sedaca is the Kelly and David Pfeil Fellow at the George W. Bush Institute.

articles.title: Swiss foreign minister talks political ties on rare visit to North Korea
articles.summary: Switzerland formally reopens diplomatic office in North Korea after its closure in 2020.
articles.body:
Switzerland has formally reopened its diplomatic office in North Korea as Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis held talks in Pyongyang about normalising political relations between the two countries.

On Friday Cassis wrapped up a two-day visit to North Korea – the first by a Swiss government minister in more than two decades – in which he discussed “regularising political relations and reestablishing a political dialogue”, he wrote on X.

Cassis, who is also Switzerland’s vice president, met Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui and Jo Yong Won, a secretary of the Central Committee of the ruling Korean Workers’ Party.

“We also exchanged views on security on the Korean Peninsula and broader Eurasian security challenges,” he added on X.

After the formal reopening of the Swiss diplomatic office on Thursday, Cassis posted that he was “pleased” to mark a “new chapter” in his country’s presence in Pyongyang, hailing the office as a “concrete step towards strengthening direct dialogue” with North Korea.

The office, operational since October 19, will not have an ambassador. It reports to the Swiss embassy in Beijing, which handles diplomatic and consular relations with North Korea. The office had closed in March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.

“This office will help to strengthen direct contacts with the authorities of the DPRK [Democratic People’s Republic of Korea] and support political dialogue with them,” the Swiss Foreign Ministry said.

North Korea’s state news agency KCNA confirmed Cassis’s arrival in the country on Thursday but gave no details on the purpose of the visit. It had not been known beforehand whether he would meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un , and there has been no report of a meeting.

Bern said it intended to maintain its commitment to the region amid heightened tensions and limited international contact with North Korea, having been one of the few Western countries to keep up a dialogue with Pyongyang.

The last Swiss Federal Council member to visit was then-Foreign Minister Micheline Calmy-Rey, in 2003.

Cassis crossed into South Korea on Friday for the final leg of his regional trip.

According to the Swiss foreign ministry, his talks in Seoul will focus on security on the peninsula, prospects for easing regional tensions and bilateral ties.

Switzerland’s involvement on the Korean Peninsula dates back more than 70 years, including its role on the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission.

Also in South Korea, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz invoked his country’s reunification during a visit to the inter-Korean border. “Let us hope that Korea, too, will one day have the chance to regain its national unity,” he said.

articles.title: Census 2027: Population enumeration from Jan 25-Feb 28 2027; poll-bound, snow-bound areas excluded
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Population enumeration for the 2027 Census will be conducted across most of India from January 25 to February 28, 2027, with poll-bound states
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Population enumeration for the 2027 Census will be conducted across most of India from January 25 to February 28, 2027, with poll-bound states and snow-bound regions excluded from the schedule, the government announced on Friday.According to a notification issued by Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, Registrar General of India and Census Commissioner, the reference date for the census will be midnight on March 1, 2027, PTI reported.The enumeration will not be conducted during this period in Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Ladakh, or in the snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.The schedule for Manipur will be announced separately. A revisional round will be held from March 1 to March 5, 2027.The government will also offer a self-enumeration option from January 10 to January 24, ahead of the house-to-house population count.Assembly elections are due in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur early next year.Census 2027: Two phasesThe 2027 Census, the eighth since Independence, will be conducted in two phases: house listing and housing census, followed by population enumeration.The decennial exercise was originally scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the Covid-19 pandemic. The Union Cabinet has approved Rs 11,718 crore for conducting the census.The Registrar General of India had announced last month that house-listing operations for Census 2027 in Manipur had been deferred.The census is a nationwide exercise to collect, compile and analyse information about the population and its demographic, social and economic characteristics.The data provides the government with a detailed picture of the country's population and living conditions.The government has said that information collected during the census will remain confidential and be used only for statistical purposes.India's last census was conducted in 2011, when the country's population stood at 1.21 billion, including 62.32 crore males and 58.75 crore females. articles.title: Egyptian highway billboard hacked to show porn
articles.summary: A billboard stretching across one of Egypt’s biggest highways in Cairo was hacked on Thursday to broadcast pornographic footage, according to the government and local media.
articles.body: A billboard stretching across one of Egypt’s biggest highways was hacked on Thursday to broadcast pornographic footage, according to the government and local media. The advertisement billboard, which sits on the bustling 26th of July Axis in Cairo, made waves on social media as many people stopped their cars and pulled out their phones to record. Footage shared on social media showed writing on the pornographic video saying, “Leaked by: Ch, 19ylegal never and nivex” and the name of a Telegram channel with the username @LeakersGov. On Friday, the account posted the message: “Egypt remains under a dictatorship. The government maintains its power through repression, while the country struggles to move forward. Years pass, but nothing changes and people’s lives don’t improve.” Egypt has functioned under military-led rule since the overthrow of the Muslim Brotherhood in 2013. Egypt’s interior ministry said the screen belonged to an advertising firm that had a contract with an international company. “The international company’s website was subjected to a cyberattack, which resulted in the unauthorized footage being broadcast,” the ministry said, adding that the breach took place “in several other countries, simultaneously.” The ministry did not identify the company, nor did it say which other countries were affected. But there are local media reports of sexually explicit footage being broadcast on electronic billboards in Iraq, Malaysia and Brazil. “Legal proceedings have been initiated,” it said. Responses on social media were mixed, with many expressing shock while some found the incident funny. Much of Egypt’s society is highly conservative, championing strict moral codes that align with Islamic sharia law. Local authorities in the region have previously been compelled to switch off electronic advertising boards after pornographic footage was broadcast on the screens. Egyptian courts have tried blocking pornographic websites, but private online access remains widespread. In fact, the North African country was among the top 20 countries visiting pornography websites in 2025, according to Pornhub Insights. The United States ranked first.

articles.title: Indian national jailed for 8 years in US over laundering case targeting elderly people; ordered to pay $2.4m to victims
articles.summary: Ahmed Maqbul Syed, an Indian citizen, was sentenced to 8 years in prison for laundering money from fraud schemes targeting elderly victims, ordered to repay $2.4 million in restitution.
articles.body: An Indian national has been sentenced to eight years in prison in the United States for helping launder money collected through fraud schemes that targeted elderly people across the country.Ahmed Maqbul Syed, 60, a former Illinois resident, received a 96-month prison sentence on Tuesday. He was also ordered to pay approximately $2.4 million in restitution to victims after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering.According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Arizona, Syed was involved in a network that handled money obtained through fraudulent tech support and government impersonation schemes. The scams targeted people across the US.The fraud typically began with fake computer alerts warning users about technical problems or freezing their devices. People who called the numbers displayed in these messages were connected to criminals posing as technical support staff or government officials.The scammers falsely told victims that their bank accounts had been hacked or their personal information compromised. In some cases, they claimed that victims' accounts were connected to child pornography or other criminal activity.Victims were then instructed to move their money to supposedly secure their assets. Some were told to purchase gold or withdraw cash and hand it over to people posing as government officials. Others were asked to buy gift cards and share their numbers with the scammers. At least one victim was directed to deposit cash into a Bitcoin ATM.The schemes resulted in substantial financial losses, with some victims losing most of their life savings, according to prosecutors.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump gives reporter fitness lecture as MAGA loses shape
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: Four days before a midterm election that could leave him politically out of shape, US President Donald Trump decided to
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: Four days before a midterm election that could leave him politically out of shape, US President Donald Trump decided to conduct a fitness assessment --- of a Reuters journalist. Faced with an innocuous question about why he was cancelling campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa, the MAGA boss erupted into an unsolicited lecture on the journalist's weight, appearance, and general state of health, betraying frayed nerves that do not augur well for his party.“You are a sick guy! Reuters is terrible, by the way. Look at this guy... he's way out of shape... You are disgusting! Put yourself in shape! You look like hell!” Trump exploded at the reporter, pushing back at any suggestion that he was tired or backing out of rallies because of heckling and poor attendance. He said he felt great and the reason he was not going to those states was because Republican candidates were doing very well and his energies were better devoted elsewhere.The exchange was not merely an illustration of a President with an unusually short fuse that has been sizzling lately; it was also a revealing snapshot of a leader entering the final stretch of an election campaign with considerably more anxiety than his public bravado suggests. Polls show Democratic candidates leading, tied, or narrowing margins in the most unexpected places, including ruby red states Trump won by 10 to 20 points in the 2024 Presidential elections.For instance, in Kansas, a state that has not elected a Democrat Senator since 1932, polls put Democrat Adam Hamilton ahead of incumbent Roger Marshall 49-45. Texas, which last elected a Democrat Senator in 1988 and which Trump carried comfortably in 2024, has become a genuine Senate battleground, with Democrat James Talarico -- who incidentally was ladling out dosas on Thursday in an effort to court Indian-American votes --- ahead of Republican Ken Paxton. South Carolina, where Republican Darline Graham is hoping to succeed her late brother Lindsay Graham as senator, has also tightened considerably.Even more unnerving for Republicans are the warning signs from states that have traditionally been considered political fortresses, including Louisiana and Mississippi, which last elected a Democratic senator in 1982. If Dems win all these races, they would be on track to reverse the Republicans’ 53-47 control of the Senate,A Democratic takeover of both chambers would leave Trump facing not merely hostile congressional hearings but chambers capable of blocking appointments, frustrating legislation, and investigating an administration dogged by allegations of cronyism and self-enrichment.Republicans, naturally, have a theory about why the polls are wrong: the hidden Trump voter. They argue that there are millions of Trump supporters who refuse to participate in polls, conceal their preferences or simply do not admit to pollsters that they intend to vote Republican. They will emerge, the theory goes, on Election Day and deliver the customary surprise.But hoping for invisible voters is not quite the same as having visible enthusiasm. In fact, some of the most visible activity at recent Trump rallies has been distinctly uncomfortable for the president and his MAGA faithful. Hecklers have interrupted Trump's speeches at rallies and his surrogates have been pranked on several occasions. At an Ohio rally, a comedian who goes by the name Robby Roadsteamer managed to interrupt Trump with a reference to Jeffrey Epstein, before being escorted out amid chants of "USA!USA!" a standard MAGA response. The president's explanation was that such protesters were paid by radical left political enemies. Roadstreamer meanwhile took credit for Trump's subsequent cancellation of the Kansas and Iowa appearances, announcing online: “Trump cancelled the rest of his rallies! You're welcome, America.” Trump allies, including Vivek Ramaswamy and Fox News, have also been punked by pranksters, who present themselves as MAGA loyalists before turning on them on camera.Trump's own response to the heckling and harsh scrutiny by the mainstream media has been to crank the personal insults up another notch, with consequent blowback that is raising political temperature all around. When he suggested that Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed should have to pass through a metal detector before entering the Senate (suggesting he is a jihadist who cannot be trusted), the Michigan Democrat clapped back: “I'll go through a metal detector if you'll sit for a lie detector” -- to answer questions about his ties to Epstein. Trump has also repeatedly disparaged Texas' Democratic candidate James Talarico as "Tala-freako" -- part of his chronic habit of name-calling.There is a broader political backdrop to the president's increasingly irritable demeanour. His administration is facing mounting accusations of corruption, grift, and self-dealing, while its aggressive efforts to influence election processes have raised questions about whether Trump is prepared to accept an adverse outcome in the election. Past record does not inspire any great confidence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
