articles.title: This Mason Jar Green Pea Salad Is Going Viral: A Dietitian’s Honest Review
articles.summary: Health and wellness influencer Raven Ross’ fiber-packed green pea and chicken salad is going viral on TikTok. A dietitian gives her honest review of the trend.
articles.body: Look, as a Southerner, I love a good chicken-fried steak as much as anyone. A proper biscuit is one of my life’s greatest delights, and those layered gelatin desserts represent a sizeable chunk of my sparkling personality. But the classic Southern pea salad of my youth, with the dull green legumes, all that mayo goop and the soggy little cheddar cubes? I’m sorry, it’s the devil’s boba pearl sundae. No thank you. So imagine my surprise when I saw that pea salad is trending on social media! Surely that stuff is irredeemable? Well, 1.3 million viewers on TikTok and a lot of imitators would beg to differ. This new take on a very old, um, favorite is the brainchild of health and wellness entrepreneur and “Love Is Blind” star Raven Ross. With technique strongly reminiscent of Logan Moffit, the cucumber salad guy, she takes an outrageous serving of warmed frozen peas, adds cubed rotisserie chicken, olive oil, Parmesan, lemon, salt and pepper, and shakes it up in a Mason jar before digging in with a spoon. Bright green, glop-free salad? Count me in! Since then, she’s become something of a pea influencer, with several quick recipes that add peas to curry sauce, pasta and her Chipotle order. She has even appeared in a hilarious pea costume to promote her favorite high-fiber ingredient. You’ve got to admire that level of commitment to the bit. I caught up with Ross to ask her about her passion for peas, and some details about ratios. Did she design this recipe with a love of Southern green pea salad from her formative years in mind? “No!” she says. “I hated it. I think it’s the texture.” (Same, girl, same.) Ross tells me she had posted about peas before by way of encouraging followers to make sure they’re getting enough fiber, but those posts hadn’t really caught on. “Then I saw someone’s really interesting but really difficult pea recipe. I think she might have had pesto in it,” she remembers. “My whole shtick is that I hate to cook but still want to eat healthy. I just felt let down because I knew I was never going to be able to do that [complicated recipe].” Instead, she was inspired to try to make things easier and see how it went — and this time, it went viral. She says she uses a whole bag of peas for a single entree-sized serving and enjoys eating this one warm, although she prefers her “salmon sushi peas” cold. As for the amounts of the seasonings, “I don’t have a cooking bone in my body,” she says, so there’s no measuring. She just adds lemon and Parm until it has the flavor she personally wants. There are lots of copycats, too, but there has been a general coalescence around an alternate version that includes Greek yogurt as a dressing and has a much higher chicken-to-peas ratio. Let’s try it! I’ve got the ingredients for Ross’ original, goopless version, and then some Icelandic yogurt and mustard I can add to taste the alternative version. I really like her tip of defrosting the peas in the microwave, shaking up along with the other ingredients and then eating it, all right out of the jar. I’m going with a cup-and-a-half of peas, closer to Ross’ original than the internet consensus but not quite as pea-forward as a whole 16-ounce bag. It doesn’t look quite as pretty once the Parm mixes with the oil, but it tastes divine. I ended up adding all of the juice from half a lemon. It’s bright, slightly sweet and filling. Peas typically fall into the “they’re fine, I guess” category for me, but I really love this and will definitely make it again — probably tomorrow! Now for the yogurt-dressed version. Some shred the chicken or add a little red onion for color. A few go all out with things like avocado, boiled eggs or capers, but that’s in opposition to Ross’s intent. “Theirs look good, but it’s more advanced than what I’m doing,” she explains. “My point is to show how easily you can do it.” So, I’m keeping it simple and just adding about 3 tablespoons of yogurt and a heaping teaspoon of Dijon mustard. I love Ross’ fresh, springy original, but I might prefer the yogurt one. I really dig the mustard tang, which keeps the peas from being too heavy on the palate. The yogurt also adds protein and calcium, but Ross’ take is a nutritional powerhouse in its own right. Either one is a great choice for lunch, hot or cold. Speaking of nutrition, some of the claims sound a little overblown, but Ross’ whole bag of peas version really does clock in at a highly respectable 50 grams of protein and 15-20 grams of fiber, depending on the brand. And although some of the commenters are concerned about the calories and carbs because it contains so many peas, their fears are unfounded; roughly 575 calories and 45 grams of delicious carbs is beyond reasonable for such a satisfying plate — I mean, jar. Are you as fired up about peas as I am now? Ross’ app has a new dedicated page with her recipes handy for clicking, and there are some great ones right here on TODAY.com, too: This pasta salad makes it easy being green, with frozen peas, asparagus and a super-herby dressing. Use a whole wheat orzo for a little extra nutritional boost. Not a fan of the subtle pop of whole peas? People often joke about pea soup, but it’s actually delicious and very easy to make. If you already love tomato shakshuka, try this green one that’s based on green peas and tomatillo salsa instead. Dinner doesn’t get healthier or more delicious than seared salmon with lightly mashed, bright green peas on the side. When pea shoots are out of season, arugula makes a similarly textured substitution. No matter which recipe you choose, I really hope you give peas a chance.

articles.title: Party Rock Anthem singer Lauren Bennett struggled with mental health, inquest finds
articles.summary: Lauren Bennett, who featured on LMFAO's hit song, was found dead by her husband.
articles.body:
A British singer who was a member of the girl group G.R.L took her own life, an inquest has found.

Lauren Bennett, 36, who also featured on LMFAO's 2011 hit Party Rock Anthem, was found dead in Kent on 29 May.

In a statement read out by an assistant coroner on Friday, her husband Kenny Wormald said she had been struggling with severe mental health issues before her death.

The court heard she told him she was going out for a walk on the morning of her death while he remained in bed half asleep.

When she did not return for a few hours and did not answer calls or texts from him and multiple other family members, Wormald and her father went looking for her.

If you have been affected by this story, you can find organisations which offer help and information at the BBC Action Line

He went to a rural location using Find My iPhone for Bennett's device where he found her body.

The professional dancer said the pair talked about everything and there was no indication she was going to end her life.

Her father, Richard Bennett, said his daughter had lived an "amazing life" in a statement read out by assistant coroner Jyoti Gill.

He said she signed a record deal at just 17 and moved to the US on her own.

Pages of farewell notes were later found at her home, Kent and Medway Coroners' Court heard.

Bennett had previously been diagnosed with Fragile X syndrome, a genetic disorder that can cause anxiety, mood instability and depression, it was also told.

In the January before her death, the musician did not sleep for a number of days and was admitted to hospital under a mental health section.

She had experienced "substantial psychological suffering" since this point, Gill noted.

Bennett was in the care of "special mental health services" at the time of her death.

She had reacted poorly to medication and did not think she was going to get better, the court was told.

No alcohol or illicit drugs were found in Bennett's system when she died.

Bennett's former musical group G.R.L. shared the news of her death on its Instagram account in July.

"Our hearts are broken, and we cannot begin to express how much she meant to us," they said.

Party Rock Anthem has been named the fifth most successful song of all time by Billboard after spending six weeks as the number one song on its Hot 100 in 2011.

Bennett also featured alongside LMFAO members in the song's music video, which has more than 2.5bn views on YouTube.

Additional reporting by Press Association.

articles.title: City of London leader named 'most influential black Briton'
articles.summary: Ian Thomas, who heads the City of London Corporation, tops the Black Powerlist in its 21st year.
articles.body:
Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the UK's most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards.

The 57-year old is the first Black person to oversee the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history.

The City of London Corporation is an administrative body with responsibility for London's central financial district, headed by its own Lord Mayor.

Thomas tops the 2027 Black Powerlist, which recognises the most powerful people of African and Caribbean heritage in the UK.

The award body said he was "a respected public-service leader with over 30 years' experience in local government".

Other influential names in this year's top ten include entrepreneurs Emma Grede and Steven Bartlett, as well as actor and filmmaker Sir Idris Elba.

Comedian Sir Lenny Henry has also been recognised, with a Lifetime Achievement award, for co-founding Comic Relief, which has raised over £1.6bn since 1985.

Now in its 21st year, the Black Powerlist celebrates people who have broken through barriers to reach leadership roles, thereby inspiring future generations.

"It exists to show young people of African and Caribbean heritage what is possible, in fields they might never have considered," said Michael Eboda, the list's publisher.

Thomas said he secured the role at the head of the City of London Corporation in 2022 only following seven interviews and an election.

'When I started my journey in public service, I never, ever thought, [not] in a million years, that I'd be recognised in this way," he told the BBC.

As chief executive, he oversees around 5,000 staff with responsibilities including the City of London Police, 11,000 acres of open spaces such as Epping Forest and Hampstead Heath, and advocacy for the UK's financial and professional services sector.

Thomas was born in Sheffield to parents who made the city their home after leaving Jamaica as part of the Windrush generation.

"They worked incredibly hard and instilled that sense of discipline and respect, and that's the core of how I do business," he said of his upbringing.

Growing up, Thomas aspired to be a footballer and took part in trials alongside Alan Shearer.

Reflecting on his own change of direction, Thomas joked it was about "following dreams and if they don't come true… there's always something else".

Before joining the City of London Corporation, Thomas served as chief executive of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames where he oversaw public services and a £1.2bn regeneration programme.

He was appointed a CBE in the 2019 New Year Honours in the wake of the Rotherham Abuse scandal for transforming children's services during his time as strategic director for children and young people at Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council.

Thomas replaces last year's incumbent, Afua Kyei, the Bank of England's chief financial officer and executive director, and is joined on this year's list by Comfort Ero, the President and chief executive of the International Crisis Group, who takes second place.

articles.title: 3 killed, 5 injured at popular tourist hot spot after rocks suddenly tumble down
articles.summary: Heavy rain triggered a deadly rockfall from a volcanic "fairy chimney" formation at Cappadocia, one of Turkey's most famous tourist destinations. Three people died; five were wounded.
articles.body: At least three people were killed at Cappadocia, a popular tourist destination in central Turkey, when a rockfall occurred Thursday, officials said. The rockfall took place at around 3:15 p.m. local time that day, according to Reuters. After the area experienced heavy rain, the rockfall came from a volcanic geological formation called a "fairy chimney," the same source said. TEEN DIES AFTER FALLING FROM MOVING CARNIVAL RIDE AS QUESTIONS MOUNT OVER SAFETY The name comes from the tall, narrow, often cone-shaped rock formations that resemble chimneys, with the "fairy" reference tied to local folklore. Rock fragments from the fairy chimney broke off and fell onto people near the Goreme Open-Air Museum, Nevsehir Gov. Huseyin Kok told reporters. Three people died and five were injured, according to The Associated Press. TOURIST DANGLES 23 STORIES ABOVE STREET IN ‘RECKLESS’ DAREDEVIL STUNT "We hope that there are no other casualties," Kok said, according to AP. "We are deeply saddened." Kok said two of the three people killed were Turkish nationals but did not provide information about the third individual, the AP reported. Rescue teams were searching through rubble at the rockfall, according to the governor. articles.title: Daund MLA Rahul Kul writes to CM on releasing water from Mulshi dam into Bhima river to benefit drought-hit areas
articles.summary: Daund MLA Rahul Kul urges CM Devendra Fadnavis to release Mulshi dam water into Mula-Mutha and Bhima rivers to ease drought in Pune-Solapur.
articles.body: Pune: Daund MLA Rahul Kul has written a letter to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on the release of water from Mulshi dam into Mula-Mutha river and Bhima river to benefit drought-hit areas of Pune and Solapur districts.The MLA has urged the CM to hold a meeting on priority to discuss the proposal, which can extend some respite to the areas that have recorded scanty rain during monsoon.Kul represents the Daund area, where deficient monsoon was recorded this year. He told TOI, “Our area primarily gets water from dams in Khadakwasla circle. However, the water levels in four dams in the circle are significantly down as compared to last year’s storages. To overcome possible water scarcity areas around Daund and Indapur will face during summer days, a proposal has been tabled to draw water from Mulshi dam. We have approached the CM on the proposal to discuss how much water can be released.”Water released from Mulshi dam will flow into Mula river, then Mula-Mutha and then Bhima rivers. Kul said that water released in these rivers will get collected in Ujani dam, located on the boundary of Pune and Solapur districts. The release will not only push up water levels in Ujani, but will also benefit villages located along these rivers by recharging groundwater level and wells.The proposal to draw water from Mulshi for drinking purposes has been under discussion at state govt level since the last few years. Kul said that the proposal has moved ahead on technical parameters. If worked out well, it will provide huge relief to urban and rural pockets in the district.Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has already mooted before state govt to provide water from Mulshi to the city to meet increasing water demand.Sources from rural areas said that water release from Khadakwasla into the irrigation canal is likely to dip in the coming winter and summer seasons due to less stock. articles.title: Government approves Sea Link cable between Kent and Suffolk
articles.summary: Critics say the plans will harm the environment, while others say it will help improve the grid.
articles.body:
A major new undersea electricity cable linking Kent and Suffolk has been approved by the government.

The Sea Link project will help carry electricity generated by offshore wind farms, interconnectors and nuclear power stations to strengthen the grid.

The 138km cable will run beneath the North Sea between Pegwell Bay in Kent and the Suffolk coast near Aldeburgh and Thorpeness.

Conservationists have raised concerns that the plans could impact wildlife, sensitive coastal habitats and the wider landscape.

National Grid said the scheme would be capable of carrying enough electricity to power the equivalent of two million homes.

The project is designed to transport up to 2GW of low-carbon electricity from where it is generated to homes and businesses elsewhere in the country.

The government said the scheme would help ease pressure on the electricity network and reduce the need to pay generators to switch off power that cannot be carried on the grid.

It said the project would support efforts to improve energy security and cut reliance on fossil fuels.

Kent Wildlife Trust said it was "deeply disappointed" by the decision.

"We recognise the need to upgrade the electricity network to support the transition to a low-carbon future," a spokesperson said.

"However, there is a profound irony in destroying or degrading the very natural habitats that help us tackle climate change and protect us from its impacts."

The Planning Inspectorate said it had listened to local views and fully considered the evidence gathered before making its recommendation.

Kent Wildlife Trust said it would "continue to challenge the project and hold those responsible to account".

"We owe it to future generations to ensure that the consequences of this decision are not overlooked."
